On Error GoTo %%Object Name::Sheet%%s_SaveModifiedErr
    Dim rs As rdoResultset
    Dim objCur As C%%Object Name%%
    Dim NextID As Long

%%Object Name%%s_SaveModified_Start_Over:
    For Each objCur In mCol

                   Set rs = db.OpenResultset("SELECT * FROM %%Table Name::Sheets%% WHERE %%AutoNumber Field Name::lSheetID%%=" & .ID, rdOpenDynamic, rdConcurValues)

                   Remove .Key

                   Set rs = db.OpenResultset("SELECT * FROM %%Table Name%% WHERE %%AutoNumber Field Name%%=" & .ID, rdOpenDynamic, rdConcurValues)

Public Function bGetTokenPhrase(sOrigStr As String, sPhrase As String, sTokenPhrase As String) As Long
    Static sStr As String
    Static nTokenPhraseStart As Long
    Static sTwoPercents As String

    sTwoPercents = Chr(37) & Chr(37)

    sStr = sOrigStr
    nTokenPhraseStart = InStr(UCase(sStr), UCase(sPhrase))
    If nTokenPhraseStart = 0 Then
     ' Phrase not present, return blank token phrase and False
       sTokenPhrase = gsB
       Exit Function
    End If

    sStr = Trim(Mid(sStr, nTokenPhraseStart + Len(sPhrase)))
    
  ' The needed token is there
    bGetTokenPhrase = True

  ' Extract the proper Token phrase if available
    If Len(sStr) = 0 Then
       sTokenPhrase = gsB
    ElseIf Left(sStr, 1) = gsA Then
       sStr = Mid(sStr, 2)
       sTokenPhrase = sExtractToken(sStr, 1, gsA)
    ElseIf Left(sStr, 1) = gsBO Then
       sStr = Mid(sStr, 2)
       sTokenPhrase = sExtractToken(sStr, 1, gsBC)
    ElseIf Left(sStr, 2) = sTwoPercents Then
       sStr = Mid(sStr, 3)
       sTokenPhrase = sExtractToken(sStr, 1, sTwoPercents)
    Else
       sTokenPhrase = gsB
    End If

  ' Modify the incoming string without the returned token
    If nTokenPhraseStart > 1 Then
       sOrigStr = Left(sOrigStr, nTokenPhraseStart - 1) & sStr
    Else
       sOrigStr = sStr
    End If

End Function

' ********************************************************************************
' Name              BrowseForFolder
'
' Parameters
'      hWndOwner                     (I)  Window handle of owner
'      sPrompt                       (I)  Browse window caption
'
' Description
'
' Allows the user to "browse" for a directory (32 bit only!!!)
'
' ********************************************************************************
Public Function BrowseForFolder(ByVal hWndOwner As Long, ByVal sPrompt As String) As String
    Dim iNull As Integer
    Dim lpIDList As Long
    Dim lResult As Long
    Dim sPath As String
    Dim udtBI As BrowseInfo

    With udtBI
         .hWndOwner = hWndOwner
         .lpszTitle = sPrompt
         .ulFlags = BIF_RETURNONLYFSDIRS
    End With

    lpIDList = SHBrowseForFolder(udtBI)
    If lpIDList Then
       sPath = String(MAX_PATH, 0)
       lResult = SHGetPathFromIDList(lpIDList, sPath)
       Call CoTaskMemFree(lpIDList)
       iNull = InStr(sPath, vbNullChar)
       If iNull Then
          sPath = Left(sPath, iNull - 1)
       End If
    End If

    BrowseForFolder = sPath

End Function

Public Function GetFiles(ByVal sSpec As String, sFiles() As String) As Integer
    Dim nFiles As Integer
    Dim sFile As String
    ReDim sFiles(1 To 10) As String

    sFile = Dir(sSpec)
    Do While Len(sFile)
       nFiles = nFiles + 1
       sFiles(nFiles) = sFile
       If nFiles = UBound(sFiles) Then
          ReDim Preserve sFiles(1 To UBound(sFiles) + 10) As String
        End If
        sFile = Dir
    Loop

    If nFiles Then
       ReDim Preserve sFiles(1 To nFiles) As String
    End If

    GetFiles = nFiles
End Function

' ***********************************************************************************
' Synopsis          Returns the number of tokens as delimited by siDelim
'
' Parameters
'
'   sAllTokens                 (I) Required. The string containing all the tokens
'   siDelim                     (I) Optional. The delimiter string that separates
'                                   the tokens. DEFAULT = " "
' Description
'  For the following:
'    sAllTokens         sDelim  Returns       Notes
'   "William M Rawls"    " "     3             "William", "M", and "Rawls"
'   "William M Rawls"    "iam"   2             "Will" and " M Rawls"
'   "William M Rawls"    ""      1             No delimiter? String has one token,
'                                              "William M Rawls"
'   "1.00.05"            "."     3             "1", "00", and "05"
' ***********************************************************************************
Public Function lTokenCount(ByVal sAllTokens As String, Optional ByVal siDelim As String = " ") As Long
    Static iCurTokenLocation As Long ' Character position of the first delimiter string
    Static iTokensSoFar As Integer      ' Used to keep track of how many tokens we've counted so far
    Static iDelim As Integer            ' Length of the delimiter string

    iDelim = Len(siDelim)
    If iDelim < 1 Then
     ' Empty delimiter strings means only one token equal to the string
       iTokenCount = 1
       Exit Function
    ElseIf Len(sAllTokens) = 0 Then
     ' Empty input string means no tokens
       Exit Function
    Else
     ' Count the number of tokens
       iTokensSoFar = 0
       Do
          iCurTokenLocation = InStr(sAllTokens, siDelim)
          If iCurTokenLocation = 0 Then
             iTokenCount = iTokensSoFar + 1 'Abs(Len(sAllTokens) > 0)
             Exit Function
          End If
          iTokensSoFar = iTokensSoFar + 1
          sAllTokens = Mid(sAllTokens, iCurTokenLocation + iDelim)
       Loop
    End If
End Function

' *********************************************************************************************
' Synopsis          Returns everything AFTER the Nth Token from sAllTokens delimited by sDelim
'
' Parameters
'
'   sAllTokens                 (I) Required. The string containing all the tokens
'   iToken                      (I) Optional. The index of the token to use as an "after" ref
'                                   DEFAULT = 1
'   siDelim                     (I) Optional. The delimiter string that separates
'                                   the tokens. DEFAULT = " "
' Description
'  For the following:
'    sAllTokens         iToken   sDelim  Returns           Notes
'   "William M Rawls"    1       " "     "M Rawls"          After the first word
'   "William M Rawls"    2       " "     "Rawls"            After the second word
'   "William M Rawls"    3       " "     ""                 After the third word (nothing)
'   "William M Rawls"    0       " "     "William M Rawls"  After zeroth token is always the input string
'   "William M Rawls"   -1       " "     "William M Rawls"  Negative tokens act same as zero
'   "William M Rawls"    1       ""      "William M Rawls"  Same as one
' *********************************************************************************************
Public Function sAfter(ByVal sAllTokens As String, Optional ByVal iToken As Integer = 1, Optional ByVal sDelim As String = " ") As String
    Static iCurTokenLocation As Long ' Character position of the first delimiter string
    Static nDelim As Integer            ' Length of the delimiter string
    
    nDelim = Len(sDelim)
    If iToken < 1 Or nDelim < 1 Then
     ' Negative or zeroth token or empty delimiter strings mean an empty token
       sAfter = sAllTokens
       Exit Function
    ElseIf iToken = 1 Then
     ' Quickly extract the first token
       iCurTokenLocation = InStr(sAllTokens, sDelim)
       If iCurTokenLocation > 1 Then
          sAfter = Mid(sAllTokens, iCurTokenLocation + nDelim)
          Exit Function
       ElseIf iCurTokenLocation = 0 Then
          sAfter = ""
          Exit Function
       Else
          sAfter = Mid(sAllTokens, nDelim + 1)
          Exit Function
       End If
    Else
     ' Find the Nth token
       Do
          iCurTokenLocation = InStr(sAllTokens, sDelim)
          If iCurTokenLocation = 0 Then
             Exit Function
          Else
             sAllTokens = Mid(sAllTokens, iCurTokenLocation + nDelim)
          End If
          iToken = iToken - 1
       Loop Until iToken = 1

     ' Extract the Nth token (Which is the next token at this point)
       iCurTokenLocation = InStr(sAllTokens, sDelim)
       If iCurTokenLocation > 0 Then
          sAfter = Mid(sAllTokens, iCurTokenLocation + nDelim)
          Exit Function
       Else
          Exit Function
       End If
    End If
End Function

'
' On Return:
'    sExtractToken
'       Token # nToken
'    sOrigStr
'       Token # (1 through nToken-1) & (nToken+1 through nTokenCount(sOrigStr))
'
' Notes:
'    Yes there are a lot of "Exit Function" statements...
'       That's to make the function return as quickly as possible
'
Public Function sExtractToken(sOrigStr$, ByVal nToken%, strDelim$)

    Static strIn$, nCurrTokenStart%, nNextTokenStart%, nLenDelim%
    Static strOut$

  ' Handle the "simple" cases (No delimiter, or token # less than 2)
    nLenDelim = Len(strDelim)
    If nToken < 1 Or nLenDelim = 0 Then
     ' Nothing to extract, return nothing
       Exit Function
    ElseIf nToken = 1 Then
       nCurrTokenStart = InStr(sOrigStr, strDelim)
       If nCurrTokenStart > 0 Then
          sExtractToken = Left(sOrigStr, nCurrTokenStart - 1)
          sOrigStr = Trim(Mid(sOrigStr, nCurrTokenStart + nLenDelim))
          Exit Function
       Else
          sExtractToken = sOrigStr
          sOrigStr = gsB
          Exit Function
       End If
    End If

  ' Find the start of then nToken'th Token
    strIn = sOrigStr: strOut = gsB
    nToken = nToken - 1
    Do Until nToken = 0
       nCurrTokenStart = InStr(strIn, strDelim)
       If nCurrTokenStart = 0 Or Len(strIn) = 0 Then Exit Function
       strOut = strOut & Left(strIn, nCurrTokenStart)
       strIn = Mid(strIn, nCurrTokenStart + nLenDelim)

     ' Check to see if this is the one the calling function is looking for
       nToken = nToken - 1
    Loop

  ' Now we're at the point" & gsWhere & "the token sought for resides
    nCurrTokenStart = InStr(strIn, strDelim)
    If nCurrTokenStart > 0 Then
       If nCurrTokenStart > 1 Then
          sExtractToken = Left(strIn, nCurrTokenStart - 1)
       Else
          sExtractToken = gsB
       End If
     ' Rewrite the original string without the last token
       sOrigStr = Trim(strOut & Mid(strIn, nCurrTokenStart + nLenDelim))
       Exit Function
    Else
       sExtractToken = strIn
       sOrigStr = Trim(strOut)
       Exit Function
    End If
End Function

'   "William M Rawls"   -1       " "     ""             Negative tokesn always empty

Public Function sGetToken(ByVal sAllTokens As String, Optional ByVal iToken As Integer = 1, Optional ByVal sDelim As String = " ") As String
    Static iCurTokenLocation As Long ' Character position of the first delimiter string
    Static nDelim As Integer            ' Length of the delimiter string
    nDelim = Len(sDelim)

    If iToken < 1 Or nDelim < 1 Then
     ' Negative or zeroth token or empty delimiter strings mean an empty token
       Exit Function
    ElseIf iToken = 1 Then
     ' Quickly extract the first token
       iCurTokenLocation = InStr(sAllTokens, sDelim)
       If iCurTokenLocation > 1 Then
          sGetToken = Left(sAllTokens, iCurTokenLocation - 1)
       ElseIf iCurTokenLocation = 1 Then
          sGetToken = ""
       Else
          sGetToken = sAllTokens
       End If
       Exit Function
    Else
     ' Find the Nth token
       Do
          iCurTokenLocation = InStr(sAllTokens, sDelim)
          If iCurTokenLocation = 0 Then
             Exit Function
          Else
             sAllTokens = Mid(sAllTokens, iCurTokenLocation + nDelim)

       iCurTokenLocation = InStr(sAllTokens, sDelim)

    End If

' Name              sReplace
'
' Parameters
'      sAll                          (I)  String
'      sFind                         (I)  String
'      sReplaceWith                  (I)  String
'
' Description
'
' Replaces all occurances of one string with another.
' ********************************************************************************
Public Function sReplace(ByVal sAll As String, ByVal sFind As String, ByVal sReplaceWith As String) As String
    Dim iCurFindPos As Long
    Dim iFind As Long
    Dim sOut As String

    iFind = Len(sFind)
    iCurFindPos = InStr(sAll, sFind)
    If InStr(sReplaceWith, sFind) = 0 Then
       Do While iCurFindPos > 0
          If iCurFindPos > 1 Then
             sAll = Left(sAll, iCurFindPos - 1) & sReplaceWith & Mid(sAll, iCurFindPos + iFind)
          Else
             sAll = sReplaceWith & Mid(sAll, iCurFindPos + iFind)
          End If
          iCurFindPos = InStr(sAll, sFind)
       Loop
       sReplace = sAll
    Else
       Do While iCurFindPos > 0
          If iCurFindPos > 1 Then
             sOut = sOut & Left(sAll, iCurFindPos - 1) & sReplaceWith
             sAll = Mid(sAll, iCurFindPos + iFind)
          Else
             sOut = sOut & sReplaceWith
             sAll = Mid(sAll, iCurFindPos + iFind)
          End If
          iCurFindPos = InStr(sAll, sFind)
       Loop
       
       sReplace = sOut & sAll
    End If
End Function

    If Len(sFilename) = 0 Then

    End If

    Dim fh As Integer
    Dim sLine As String
    Dim CurAssocArray As CAssocArray

    fh = FreeFile

    If bClearFirst = True Then
       Clear
    End If
    
    Open sFilename For Input Access Read As #fh
         Do Until EOF(fh)
            Line Input #fh, sLine
            If Len(sLine) = 0 Then
             ' Skip it
            ElseIf Left(sLine, 1) = "[" Then
               Set CurAssocArray = Add(Mid(sLine, 2, Len(sLine) - 2))
               With CurAssocArray
                    Line Input #fh, sLine
                        .ItemDelimiter = sAfter(sDenormalize(sLine), 1, "=")
                    Line Input #fh, sLine
                        .KeyValueDelimiter = sAfter(sDenormalize(sLine), 1, "=")
                    Line Input #fh, sLine
                        .FieldDelimiter = sAfter(sDenormalize(sLine), 1, "=")
               End With
            Else
               CurAssocArray.Add sGetToken(sLine, 1, "="), sAfter(sLine, 1, "=")
            End If
         Loop
    Close #fh
    Set CurAssocArray = Nothing

    Dim sOldItem As String
    Dim sOldKV As String

    Open sFilename For Output Access Write As #fh
         For Each CurAssocArray In mCol
             With CurAssocArray
                  sOldItem = .ItemDelimiter
                  sOldKV = .KeyValueDelimiter
                  Print #fh, "[" & .Section & "]"

                  Print #fh, "Delimiter Field=" & sNormalize(.FieldDelimiter)

    Close #fh
    Set CurAssocArray = Nothing

                   rs.Delete

                End If

                If .ID > 0 Then ' Modify the existing record
                   Set rs = db.OpenResultset("SELECT * FROM %%Table Name%% WHERE %%AutoNumber Field Name%%=" & .ID, rdOpenDynamic, rdConcurValues)
                   rs.Edit
                   rs!DateModified = Now()
                Else            ' Create a new record
                   Set rs = db.OpenResultset("SELECT MAX(%%Table Name%%ID)+1 FROM %%Table Name%%")
                   NextID = IIF(IsNull(rs.rdoColumns(0).Value),1,rs.rdoColumns(0).Value)
                   rs.Close
                   Set rs = db.OpenResultset("SELECT * FROM %%Table Name%%", rdOpenDynamic, rdConcurValues)
                   rs.AddNew

                   rs!DateModified = Now()
                   .Parent = %%Parent AutoNumber Field Name%%
                   .ID = NextID

                   rs!%%Parent AutoNumber Field Name%% = %%Parent AutoNumber Field Name%%
                End If
                   rs!%%Key Field Name::sName%% = .Key
                .SaveProperties rs

Public Function BinToHex(bytes() As Byte) As String
    Dim saForString As SAFEARRAY1D
    Dim saForBytes As SAFEARRAY1D

    Dim saPtrForBytes As Long
    Dim psaForString() As Long
    Dim lCount As Long

  ' Get the safearray data for the passed in array. This gives us a fast
  ' mechanism to look at the dims, lower bound, and element count of the array.
    CopyMemory saPtrForBytes, ByVal VarPtrArray(bytes), 4
    CopyMemory saForBytes, ByVal saPtrForBytes, Len(saForBytes)
    
    With saForBytes
         If .cDims <> 1 Then Err.Raise 5

       ' Normalize the lower bound to 0, save calculations in loop
         If .Bounds(0).lLBound Then
            CopyMemory ByVal UnsignedAdd(saPtrForBytes, 20), 0&, 4
         End If

         If Not m_fInit Then
            CopyMemory m_psaHexPairs(0), ByVal StrPtr(cstrHexPairs), LenB(cstrHexPairs)
            m_fInit = True
         End If

       ' Allocate returned string array directly into name of function
         BinToHex = String(.Bounds(0).cElements * 2, 0)

       ' Setup safearray pointing to string we just allocated
         With saForString
              .cbElements = 4
              .cDims = 1
              .pvData = StrPtr(BinToHex)
         End With
         saForString.Bounds(0).cElements = .Bounds(0).cElements
         CopyMemory ByVal VarPtrArray(psaForString), VarPtr(saForString), 4

       ' Do the actual work to copy the hex bytes across
         lCount = .Bounds(0).cElements
         Do While lCount
            lCount = lCount - 1
            psaForString(lCount) = m_psaHexPairs(bytes(lCount))
         Loop
         
       ' NULL out array pointer
         CopyMemory ByVal VarPtrArray(psaForString), 0&, 4
         
       ' Restore old lbound
         If .Bounds(0).lLBound Then
            CopyMemory ByVal UnsignedAdd(saPtrForBytes, 20), .Bounds(0).lLBound, 4
         End If
    End With
End Function

Public Function UnsignedAdd(Start As Long, Incr As Long) As Long
      ' Only works with positive increments
        If Start And &H80000000 Then  ' Start < 0
           UnsignedAdd = Start + Incr
        ElseIf (Start Or &H80000000) < -Incr Then
           UnsignedAdd = Start + Incr
        Else
           UnsignedAdd = (Start + &H80000000) + (Incr + &H80000000)
        End If
End Function

' ******************************************************************************************
' Name              sInsertSpaces
'
' Parameters
'      sToInsertInto                 (I)  String.
'
' Returns
'      String                        .
'
' Description
'
' Inserts spaces into a string. Spaces are inserted at each capital letter.
' Common words not to be capitalized are handled automatically (a, an, the, or,
' of). The sub string "ID" is handled specially and is removed. This function is
' excellent for labels.
'
' ******************************************************************************************
Public Function sInsertSpaces(ByVal sToInsertInto As String) As String
    Dim bytOriginal() As Byte
    Dim sWithSpaces As String
    Dim nUpper As Long
    Dim nCurrent As Long
    Dim nA As Byte
    Dim nZ As Byte

    bytOriginal = StrConv(sToInsertInto, vbFromUnicode)
    nUpper = UBound(bytOriginal)
    
    For nCurrent = 0 To nUpper
        If bytOriginal(nCurrent) >= 65 And bytOriginal(nCurrent) <= 90 And nCurrent <> 0 Then
           sWithSpaces = sWithSpaces & " " & Chr(bytOriginal(nCurrent))
        Else
           sWithSpaces = sWithSpaces & Chr(bytOriginal(nCurrent))
        End If
    Next nCurrent
    
    sInsertSpaces = sReplace(sReplace(sReplace(sReplace(sReplace(sReplace(sWithSpaces, " Of ", " of "), " The ", " the "), " A ", " a "), " An ", " an "), " I D", ""), "  ", " ")
End Function

Public Function LoadFormPosition(frmToActOn As Form, Optional ByVal bAutoCenter = True)

Public Function LogError( ByVal sModuleName As String, sProcName As String, lError As Long, sErrorMsg As String) As Boolean
    Dim fh As Long
    Dim sMessage As String

    fh = FreeFile
    Open "ERRORLOG.TXT" For Append As #fh
         sMessage = "***** Error " & Format(lError, "00000") & " at: " & Format(Now(), "MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS AM/PM")
         sMessage = sMessage & Chr(13) & "  *** Module:         " & sModuleName
         sMessage = sMessage & Chr(13) & "  *** Procedure:      " & sProcName
         sMessage = sMessage & Chr(13) & "  *** Description:    " & sErrorMsg
         Print #fh, sMessage
         sMessage = sMessage & Chr(13) & Chr(13) & Chr(9) & "Continue after error ? (No to exit program)"
         If MsgBox( sMessage, vbYesNo ) = vbYes Then 
            Print #fh, "  *** Program shut down by user after error."
            ShutDownNicely
         Else
            Print #fh, "  *** Program continued by user after error."
         End If
    Close #fh

End Function

Public Function GetExceptionText(ByVal ExceptionCode As Long) As String
  Dim strExceptionString As String
  
  Select Case ExceptionCode

         Case EXCEPTION_FLT_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO:       strExceptionString = "Divide By Zero"
         Case EXCEPTION_FLT_INEXACT_RESULT:       strExceptionString = "Floating Point Inexact Result"
         Case EXCEPTION_FLT_INVALID_OPERATION:    strExceptionString = "Invalid Operation"
         Case EXCEPTION_FLT_OVERFLOW:             strExceptionString = "Float Overflow"
         Case EXCEPTION_FLT_STACK_CHECK:          strExceptionString = "Float Stack Check"
         Case EXCEPTION_FLT_UNDERFLOW:            strExceptionString = "Float Underflow"
         Case EXCEPTION_INT_DIVIDE_BY_ZERO:       strExceptionString = "Integer Divide By Zero"
         Case EXCEPTION_INT_OVERFLOW:             strExceptionString = "Integer Overflow"
         Case EXCEPTION_PRIVILEGED_INSTRUCTION:   strExceptionString = "Privileged Instruction"
         Case EXCEPTION_IN_PAGE_ERROR:            strExceptionString = "In Page Error"
         Case EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION:      strExceptionString = "Illegal Instruction"
         Case EXCEPTION_NONCONTINUABLE_EXCEPTION: strExceptionString = "Non Continuable Exception"

' MyExceptionFilter
' ******************************
'   This function will be called when an unhandled exception occurs.
'   It raises an error so that it can be trapped with an ON ERROR statement in the procedure that caused the exception.
Public Function MyExceptionFilter(ByRef ExceptionPtrs As EXCEPTION_POINTERS) As Long
   Dim Rec As EXCEPTION_RECORD
   Dim strException As String
  
 ' Get the current exception record.
   Rec = ExceptionPtrs.pExceptionRecord
  
 ' If Rec.pExceptionRecord is not zero, then it is a nested exception and
 ' Rec.pExceptionRecord points to another EXCEPTION_RECORD structure.  Follow
 ' the pointers back to the original exception.
   Do Until Rec.pExceptionRecord = 0
    ' A friendly declaration of CopyMemory.
      CopyExceptionRecord Rec, Rec.pExceptionRecord, Len(Rec)
   Loop
  
 ' Translate the exception code into a user-friendly string.
   strException = GetExceptionText(Rec.ExceptionCode)
  
 ' Raise an error to return control to the calling procedure.
   Err.Raise 10000, "MyExceptionFilter", strException
End Function

Public Const LOGERRORFAILED = EBPPAppError + 2
Public Const EXTERNALAPPERROR = EBPPAppError + 3

'******************************************************
'There are a number of methods for retrieving the error
'message.  The following method uses a resource file to
'retrieve strings indexed by the error number you are
'raising.
Public Function RaiseError(ByVal ErrorNumber As Variant, ByVal Source As Variant, ByVal MethodName As Variant, ByVal Description As Variant, Optional ByVal LineNumber As Variant, Optional ByVal CancelError As Boolean = False) As Long
    'generated Entry Code
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler

    Dim strUserMsg As String
    Dim oErrMsg As IEBPPErrorText.EBPPErrorText
    Dim strVer As String
    Dim lngUnMaskedErrorNumber As Long
    Dim ErrNum As Long
    Dim strLogAll As String
    
    strUserMsg = ""
    
    strLogAll = UCase(GetSetting(APPLICATIONNAME, "Log", DEFAULTVERBOSELOGGINGKEY))
    If strLogAll = "" Then
        Call SaveSetting(APPLICATIONNAME, "Log", DEFAULTVERBOSELOGGINGKEY, DEFAULTVERBOSELOGGING)
    End If
    
    'Not our Components
    If (ErrorNumber And EBPPExApplicationResult) <> EBPPExApplicationResult Then
        'If no one else has logged it and is not a business rule, then we will
        If (ErrorNumber And EBPPExExceptionLogged) <> EBPPExExceptionLogged Then
            'Send a Message to the log
            If Not LogError(ErrorNumber, Source, MethodName, vbCrLf & "EXTERNAL COMPONENT:" & vbCrLf & "PASSED IN DESC: " & Description) Then
                'raise error
                Err.Raise LOGERRORFAILED, "modErrorHandler.RaiseError", "The call to LogError failed for external components."
            End If
            'Mark ErrorNumber as Logged
            ErrorNumber = (ErrorNumber Or EBPPExExceptionLogged)
        End If
    Else
    'One of our Components
        
        'Add version information to string
        strVer = "(Version " & App.Major & "." & App.Minor & "." & App.Revision
        If InStr(Source, "(Version") = 0 Then
            If Not IsMissing(LineNumber) Then
                strVer = strVer & ", Line " & LineNumber
            End If
            Source = vbCrLf & Trim(Source) & "  " & strVer & ")"
        End If
        
        'Unmask the Error number to get the value
        lngUnMaskedErrorNumber = (ErrorNumber And ErrorMask) - EBPPExBusinessRule
    
        If SafeCreateObject(oErrMsg, OBJ_ERRORTEXT, ErrNum) Then
            'Call the Resource File or DB to get Error Message
            strUserMsg = oErrMsg.GetErrorText(lngUnMaskedErrorNumber)
            Set oErrMsg = Nothing
        Else
            'Raise error
            Err.Raise SAFECREATEFAILED_ERR, "modEBPPError.RaiseError" & strVer, "Failed to Create: " & OBJ_ERRORTEXT & vbCrLf & "Return Code was " & ErrNum
        End If
        
        If strUserMsg = "" Then
            strUserMsg = vbCrLf & "NO ERROR MESSAGE EXISTS for ErrorNumber: " & CStr(lngUnMaskedErrorNumber) & vbCrLf & "DESC: " & Description
            'Write record to log to create entry for text message clean-up
            If Not LogError(ErrorNumber, Source, MethodName, "CLEAN MESSAGE TEXT: (Dec:" & lngUnMaskedErrorNumber & ": Hex:" & Hex(ErrorNumber) & ")" & vbCrLf & vbCrLf & "PASSED IN DESC: " & Description) Then
                'raise error
                Err.Raise LOGERRORFAILED, "modErrorHandler.RaiseError", "The call to LogError failed for our components."
            End If
        End If
        
        If (ErrorNumber And EBPPExExceptionLogged) <> EBPPExExceptionLogged Then
            If (strLogAll = "TRUE") Or ((ErrorNumber And EBPPExBusinessRule) <> EBPPExBusinessRule) Then
                'Send a Message to the log
                If Not LogError(ErrorNumber, Source, MethodName, "INTERNAL COMPONENT: (Dec:" & lngUnMaskedErrorNumber & ": Hex:" & Hex(ErrorNumber) & ")" & vbCrLf & strUserMsg & vbCrLf & "PASSED IN DESC: " & Description) Then
                    'raise error
                    Err.Raise LOGERRORFAILED, "modErrorHandler.RaiseError", "The call to LogError failed for our components."
                End If
    
                'Mark ErrorNumber as Logged
                ErrorNumber = (ErrorNumber Or EBPPExExceptionLogged)
            End If
        End If
    End If

    'Pass it up the stream
    If Not CancelError Then
        On Error GoTo 0
        Err.Raise ErrorNumber, Source, IIf(strUserMsg = "", Description, strUserMsg)
    End If
    
    Set oErrMsg = Nothing
    
    'generated Exit Code
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
'Code to try and handle the Error

'If not Handled then Raise the Error
    Dim ErrNumber As Long
    Dim ErrSource As String
    Dim ErrDescription As String

    Set oErrMsg = Nothing

    ErrNumber = Err.Number
    ErrSource = Err.Source
    ErrDescription = Err.Description
    
    On Error GoTo 0
    Call Err.Raise(ErrNumber, ErrSource, "Method: modEBPPError.RaiseError" & vbCrLf & ErrDescription)
    Exit Function
End Function

'******************************************************
'This function is used to write out an Error Log entry to either the NT Event
'Viewer or a DB table.
'If writing to the NTEvent Log then the NT Event type should always be:
' vbLogEventTypeError     1     Error
'
'This makes it easier.
Private Function LogError(ByVal ErrorNumber As Variant, ByVal ErrorSource As Variant, ByVal ErrorMethod As Variant, ByVal ErrorDescription As Variant) As Boolean
    'generated Entry Code
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    Dim strMessage As String
    Dim strSourceName As String
    Dim strServerName As String
    Dim iLogType As LogEventTypeConstants

    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    
    LogError = False
    
    strServerName = GetSetting(APPLICATIONNAME, "Log", DEFAULTSERVERKEY)
    strSourceName = APPLICATIONNAME
    
    If strServerName = "" Then
        Call SaveSetting(APPLICATIONNAME, "Log", DEFAULTSERVERKEY, DEFAULTSERVERNAME)
    End If
   
    'Make the Error Message Readable
    strMessage = vbCrLf & "ErrorNumber: " & ErrorNumber & vbCrLf & "ErrorSource: " & ErrorSource & vbCrLf & "ErrorMethod: " & ErrorMethod & vbCrLf & "ErrorDescription: " & ErrorDescription & vbCrLf
    
    'Determine type
    If (ErrorNumber And EBPPExApplicationResult) <> EBPPExApplicationResult Then
        iLogType = vbLogEventTypeError
        ErrorNumber = DEFAULTAPPEVENTID
    ElseIf ((ErrorNumber And EBPPExBusinessRule) <> EBPPExBusinessRule) Then
        iLogType = vbLogEventTypeError
    Else
        iLogType = vbLogEventTypeWarning
    End If
     
    'Write to NT EventViewer
    'This call will pass the Error Number as the EventID. This is useful if the
    'Error is from one of our components as it will be the Unmasked Error number.
    If strServerName = "" Or strServerName = DEFAULTSERVERNAME Then
        Call LogNTEvent(strMessage, , strSourceName, iLogType, ErrorNumber)
    Else
        Call LogNTEvent(strMessage, strServerName, strSourceName, iLogType, ErrorNumber)
    End If
    
    LogError = True
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
'Code to try and handle the Error

'If not Handled then Raise the Error
    Dim ErrNumber As Long
    Dim ErrSource As String
    Dim ErrDescription As String

    ErrNumber = Err.Number
    ErrSource = Err.Source
    ErrDescription = Err.Description
    
    On Error GoTo 0
    Call Err.Raise(ErrNumber, ErrSource, "modEBPPError.LogError" & ErrDescription)
    Exit Function
End Function

Private Sub LogNTEvent(ByVal sMessage As String, Optional ByVal sServerName As String = vbNullString, Optional ByVal sSourceName As String = "EBPP", Optional ByVal iLogType As Integer = vbLogEventTypeError, Optional ByVal iEventID As Long)

On Error GoTo ErrorHandler

    Dim bRC As Boolean
    Dim iNumStrings As Integer
    Dim hEventLog As Long
    Dim hMsgs As Long
    Dim cbStringSize As Long
        
    If sServerName = "" Or IsMissing(sServerName) Then
        sServerName = ""
    End If
    
    hEventLog = RegisterEventSource(sServerName, sSourceName)
    cbStringSize = Len(sMessage) + 1
    hMsgs = GlobalAlloc(&H40, cbStringSize)
    CopyMemory ByVal hMsgs, ByVal sMessage, cbStringSize
    iNumStrings = 1
    
    'Mapped the iEventID to the Error Number
    If ReportEvent(hEventLog, iLogType, 0, iEventID, 0&, iNumStrings, cbStringSize, hMsgs, hMsgs) = 0 Then
        On Error GoTo 0
        Err.Raise LOGNTEVENTFAILED, "modErrorHandler.LogNTEvent", "modErrorHandler Bombed!!"
    End If
        
ExitRoutine:
    Call GlobalFree(hMsgs)
    DeregisterEventSource (hEventLog)
  
    Exit Sub

ErrorHandler:
    Call GlobalFree(hMsgs)
    DeregisterEventSource (hEventLog)
    On Error GoTo 0
    Err.Raise LOGNTEVENTFAILED, "modErrorHandler.LogNTEvent", "modErrorHandler Bombed!!"
    GoTo ExitRoutine
    
End Sub

'Synopsis:
'The function will validate that the characters in the Password
' are in the range of:
'   0-9 is 48 to 57
'   A-Z is 65 to 90
'   a-z is 97 to 122
'
'Function input:
' Password
'
'Function output:

Public Function ValidateCharacters(ByVal Password As String) As Boolean
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    Dim i As Integer
    Dim strTemp As String
    Dim lngMinPwdLength As Long
    Dim lngMaxPwdLength As Long
    
    ValidateCharacters = False
    
    'Check for blank
    If Password = "" Then
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    For i = 1 To Len(Password)
        'loop through each character
        strTemp = Mid(Password, i, 1)
        'Check if char in Good list
        Select Case Asc(strTemp)
        Case 48 To 57, 65 To 90, 97 To 122
            '0-9 is 48 to 57
            'A-Z is 65 to 90
            'a-z is 97 to 122
        Case Else
            'bad char
            Exit Function
        End Select

    'Check length
    Call LoadSystemParm
    lngMinPwdLength = gcolSysParm.Item(1).MinUserPwdLength
    lngMaxPwdLength = gcolSysParm.Item(1).MaxUserPwdLength
    
    If (Len(Password) < lngMinPwdLength) Or (Len(Password) > lngMaxPwdLength) Then
        'UserID is bad
        ValidateCharacters = False
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ValidateCharacters = True

'=======================================================================
'Synopsis:
'The function will validate that the characters in the EmailAddress
' have one "@" symbol and one or more ".".
'
'Function input:
' EmailAddress
'
'Function output:
' Boolean - True or False
'
'History:
'LR 5/18/99
'Changed the check to be more open. Removed checks for:
'   "-" is 45
'   0-9 is 48 to 57
'   A-Z is 65 to 90
'   "_" is 95
'   a-z is 97 to 122
'GRG 6/15/99 Added check for valid domain, and @ not first character.
'            And "-" not first or last character of domain
'
'LR 8/22/99 Added check for "spaces" and if found then return False
'   " " is 32
'=======================================================================

Public Function ValidateEmailAddress(ByVal vData As String) As Boolean
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    
    Dim i As Integer
    Dim strTemp As String
    Dim intNumDot As Integer
    Dim intNumAt As Integer
    Dim LastPeriod As String
    
    ValidateEmailAddress = False
    'validate properly formed domain
    'last character of domain cannot be a "-"
    If Right(vData, 1) = "-" Then
       Exit Function
    End If
    'first character of an email connot be the "@"
    If Left(vData, 1) = "@" Then
       Exit Function
    End If
    'find the last period
    'Note the splendid use of a down-counter
    For i = Len(vData) To 2 Step -1
       LastPeriod = Mid(vData, i, 1)
       If LastPeriod = "." Then
          Exit For
       End If
    Next i
    'email is too small
    If i < 3 Then
       Exit Function
    End If
    'take the position we found the last period, add 1, check for "-"
    If Mid(vData, i + 1, 1) = "-" Then
       Exit Function
    End If
    'check for too many @'s
    For i = 1 To Len(vData)
        'loop through each character
        strTemp = Mid(vData, i, 1)
        Select Case Asc(strTemp)
        Case 32
            '   " " is 32
            Exit Function
        Case 46
            '   "." is 46
            intNumDot = intNumDot + 1
        Case 64
            '   "@" is 64
            intNumAt = intNumAt + 1
            If intNumAt > 1 Then
                'too many @ signs
                Exit Function
            End If
        End Select
    Next
    'need at least 1 period, or 1 @ to be properly formed
    If intNumDot = 0 Or intNumAt = 0 Then
        'invalid
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ValidateEmailAddress = True
    
'generated Exit Code
    Exit Function

'If not Handled then Raise the Error
    Dim ErrNumber As Long
    Dim ErrSource As String
    Dim ErrDescription As String

    ErrNumber = Err.Number

Public Function ValidateABA(ByVal vData As String) As Boolean
   On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
   
   Dim i As Integer
   Dim intTestDigit As Integer, intSum1 As Integer, intSum2 As Integer
   Dim intSum3 As Integer, intSum4 As Integer, intSum5 As Integer
   Dim intSum6 As Integer, intSum7 As Integer, intSum8 As Integer
   Dim intTotal As Integer, intProof As Integer
   
   'check for length
   If Len(vData) < 9 Then
      Exit Function
   End If
   'check for numeric data
   For i = 1 To 9
      Select Case Val(Mid(vData, i, 1))
         Case 0 To 9
            ' We are OK.
         Case Else
            ValidateABA = False
            Exit Function
      End Select
   Next i
   'get the proof digit the user entered
   intTestDigit = Val(Right(vData, 1))
   'Modulus 10 - Straight Summation
   'multiply digits of the ABA number by our Modulus
   intSum1 = Val(Left(vData, 1)) * 3
   intSum2 = Val(Mid(vData, 2, 1)) * 7
   intSum3 = Val(Mid(vData, 3, 1)) * 1
   intSum4 = Val(Mid(vData, 4, 1)) * 3
   intSum5 = Val(Mid(vData, 5, 1)) * 7
   intSum6 = Val(Mid(vData, 6, 1)) * 1
   intSum7 = Val(Mid(vData, 7, 1)) * 3
   intSum8 = Val(Mid(vData, 8, 1)) * 7
   'determine the Sum
   intTotal = intSum1 + intSum2 + _
              intSum3 + intSum4 + _
              intSum5 + intSum6 + _
              intSum7 + intSum8
   'determine what added to the sum would take
   'the sum to the next zero
   intProof = 10 - Val(Right(CStr(intTotal), 1))
   'test if the calculated proof is the same as the
   'proof entered by the user
   If intProof = intTestDigit Then
      ValidateABA = True
   Else
      ValidateABA = False
      Exit Function
   End If
   Exit Function

    Dim ErrNumber As Long
    Dim ErrSource As String
    Dim ErrDescription As String

    ErrNumber = Err.Number
    ErrSource = Err.Source
    ErrDescription = Err.Description
    
    Call RaiseError(ErrNumber, ErrSource, "modUtility.ValidateABA", ErrDescription)
    Exit Function
   
End Function

Public Function GetPKID() As Long
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    
    Dim DALEng As IEBPPDALEng
    Dim rsUsers As ADODB.Recordset
    Dim Errors As ADODB.Errors
    Dim iCounter As Integer
    Dim bRetVal As Boolean
    
    GetPKID = 0
    
    Set DALEng = New IEBPPDALEng
    
    'Query DAL
    bRetVal = DALEng.ExecuteSP(SPNames.spBSUser_GetPKID, , , rsUsers, SYSTEMIDCODE, Errors)
    If bRetVal = False Then
        'we want to retry
        For iCounter = 1 To RETRYMAX
            bRetVal = DALEng.ExecuteSP(SPNames.spBSUser_GetPKID, , , rsUsers, SYSTEMIDCODE, Errors)
            If bRetVal = True Then
                GetPKID = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_USERSN) + INCPKIDVAULE
                Exit For
            End If
        Next
    Else
        'Worked the first time
        GetPKID = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_USERSN) + INCPKIDVAULE
    End If
    
    Set rsUsers = Nothing
    Set DALEng = Nothing

'generated Exit Code
    Exit Function

'Code to try and handle the Error

'If not Handled then Raise the Error
    Dim ErrNumber As Long
    Dim ErrSource As String
    Dim ErrDescription As String

    ErrNumber = Err.Number
    ErrSource = Err.Source
    ErrDescription = Err.Description

    Set rsUsers = Nothing
    Set DALEng = Nothing

    Call RaiseError(ErrNumber, ErrSource, "modUser.GetPKID", ErrDescription)
    Exit Function
End Function

Public Function Enroll(UserID As Variant, Password As Variant, Email As Variant, AccountNumber As Variant, ChangePassword As Boolean, Role As eEBPPSecurityRole, CICSID As String, EnrollCode As Variant, ABANumber As Variant, BankName As Variant, BankAcctNumber As Variant, BankAcctType As Variant, ByPassFlag As Variant, CodeWord As Variant, BPPFlag As Variant, CustomerName As Variant, PhoneNumber As Variant, EnrollAcctBPP As Variant) As Boolean
    Dim oCOMTI As IEBPP.CICSDA
    Dim strCOBOLRetval As String
    Dim strSQLRetVal As String
    Dim ErrNum As Long
    Dim strRetCode As String
    Dim strSYSUSRID As String
    Dim lRetVal As Long
    
    If Not SafeCreateObject(oCOMTI, OBJ_COMTIENG, ErrNum) Then
        LogEnrollment "F", "COMTI Creation Failed", UserID, AccountNumber
        Err.Raise SAFECREATEFAILED_ERR, "colUser.Update", _
            "Failed to Create: " & OBJ_COMTIENG & vbCrLf & "Return Code was " & ErrNum
    End If

    'Check Status
    If oCOMTI.REStatus <> COMTIRESTATUS Then
        LogEnrollment "F", "COMTI ReStatus Check Failed", UserID, AccountNumber
        Err.Raise USERCOMTIRESTATUSNOTVALID, "colUser.Update", "COMTI RESTATUS not valid on check."
        Exit Function
    End If
    'Good to go
    lRetVal = oCOMTI.DoEnroll(strCOBOLRetval, strRetCode, COMTITRANSACTIONKEY, _
                              strSQLRetVal, UserID, Password, Email, _
                              AccountNumber, IIf(ChangePassword, "Y", "N"), _
                              strSYSUSRID, EnrollCode, IIf(ByPassFlag, "Y", "N"), _
                              CodeWord, BPPFlag, ABANumber, _
                              BankAcctNumber, _
                              BankAcctType, BankName, _
                              Role, CICSID, CustomerName, PhoneNumber, EnrollAcctBPP)
    Set oCOMTI = Nothing
    
    If strCOBOLRetval = "F" Then
        'raise error
        Err.Raise USERCOMTIVSAMPOSTFAILED, "colUser.Update", "COMTI CALL RETURNED F. ReturnCode was: " & strRetCode & vbCrLf & "SQLReturnCode was :" & strSQLRetVal
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    'COMTI ERROR CODE
    If strRetCode <> COMTIGOODRETURNCODE Then
        'Log Enrollment attempt
        LogEnrollment LOGLOGINFAILED, "COMTI Enrollment Call Failed", UserID, AccountNumber

        Select Case strRetCode
            Case COMTIDB2FAILED
                'Raise Error
                Err.Raise USERCOMTIDB2FAILED, "colUser.Update", "DoEnroll: DB2 SQL FAILED. ReturnCode was: " & strRetCode & vbCrLf & "SQLReturnCode was :" & strSQLRetVal
                Exit Function
            Case COMTINOTVALIDTRANXCODE
                'Raise Error
                Err.Raise USERCOMTINOTVALIDTRANXCODE, "colUser.Update", "DoEnroll: COMTI INVALID TRANXCODE. ReturnCode was: " & strRetCode & vbCrLf & "SQLReturnCode was :" & strSQLRetVal
                Exit Function
            Case Else
                'something other then Constants returned
                'Raise Error
                Err.Raise USERCOMTIINVALIDRETURNCODE, "colUser.Update", "DoEnroll: INVALID RETURN CODE: ReturnCode was: " & strRetCode & vbCrLf & "SQLReturnCode was :" & strSQLRetVal
                Exit Function
            End Select
    End If

    'If no errors then
    
    LogEnrollment LOGLOGINSUCCESS, "Succesful Enrollment", UserID, AccountNumber
    Enroll = True
End Function

INFO: Microsoft Consulting Services Naming Conventions for Visual Basic

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The information in this article applies to:

Microsoft Visual Basic Standard, Professional, and Enterprise Editions, 16-bit and 32-bit, for Windows, version 4.0 
Microsoft Visual Basic Standard and Professional Editions for Windows, versions 2.0, 3.0

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


SUMMARY
It is a good idea to establish naming conventions for your Visual Basic code. This article gives you the naming conventions used by Microsoft Consulting Services (MCS). 

This document is a superset of the Visual Basic coding conventions found in the Visual Basic "Programmer's Guide." 

NOTE: The third-party controls mentioned in this article are manufactured by vendors independent of Microsoft. Microsoft makes no warranty, implied or otherwise, regarding these controls' performance or reliability. 

MORE INFORMATION
Naming conventions help Visual Basic programmers: 

	- standardize the structure, coding style and logic of an application.
	- create precise, readable, and unambiguous source code.
	- be consistent with other language conventions (most importantly, the Visual Basic Programmers Guide and standard Windows C Hungarian notation).
	- be efficient from a string size and labor standpoint, thus allowing a greater opportunity for longer and fuller object names.
	- define the minimal requirements necessary to do the above. 

Setting Environment Options
Use Option Explicit. Declare all variables to save programming time by reducing the number of bugs caused by typos (for example, aUserNameTmp vs. sUserNameTmp vs. sUserNameTemp). In the Environment Options dialog, set Require Variable Declaration to Yes. The Option Explicit statement requires you to declare all the variables in your Visual Basic program. Save Files as ASCII Text. Save form (.FRM) and module (.BAS) files as ASCII text to facilitate the use of version control systems and minimize the damage that can be caused by disk corruption. In addition, you can: 

	- use your own editor
	- use automated tools, such as grep
	- create code generation or CASE tools for Visual Basic
	- perform external analysis of your Visual Basic code 


To have Visual Basic always save files as ASCII text, from the Environment Options dialog, set the Default Save As Format option to Text. 
Object Naming Conventions for Standard Objects
The following tables define the MCS standard object name prefixes. These prefixes are consistent with those documented in the Visual Basic Programmers Guide.

NOTE: Using a suffix for queries allows each query to be sorted with its associated table in Microsoft Access dialogs (Add Table, List Tables Snapshot). 
Menu Naming Conventions
Applications frequently use an abundance of menu controls. As a result, you need a different set of naming conventions for these controls. Menu control prefixes should be extended beyond the initial mnu label by adding an additional prefix for each level of nesting, with the final menu caption at the end of the name string. For example: 

Menu Caption Sequence   Menu Handler Name
Help.Contents           mnuHelpContents
File.Open               mnuFileOpen
Format.Character        mnuFormatCharacter
File.Send.Fax           mnuFileSendFax
File.Send.Email         mnuFileSendEmail 

When this convention is used, all members of a particular menu group are listed next to each other in the object drop-down list boxes (in the code window and property window). In addition, the menu control names clearly document the menu items to which they are attached. 
Naming Conventions for Other Controls
For new controls not listed above, try to come up with a unique three character prefix. However, it is more important to be clear than to stick to three characters. 

For derivative controls, such as an enhanced list box, extend the prefixes above so that there is no confusion over which control is really being used. A lower-case abbreviation for the manufacturer would also typically be added to the prefix. For example, a control instance created from the Visual Basic Professional 3D frame could uses a prefix of fra3d to avoid confusion over which control is really being used. A command button from MicroHelp could use cmdm to differentiate it from the standard command button (cmd). 

Third-party Controls
Each third-party control used in an application should be listed in the application's overview comment section, providing the prefix used for the control, the full name of the control, and the name of the software vendor: 
Prefix    Control Type        Vendor
cmdm      Command Button      MicroHelp 

Variable and Routine Naming
Variable and function names have the following structure: <prefix><body><qualifier><suffix> 
Part          Description                                  Example
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
<prefix>      Describes the use and scope of the variable. iGetRecordNext
<body>        Describes the variable.                      iGetNameFirst
<qualifier>   Denotes a derivative of the variable.        iGetNameLast
<suffix>      The optional Visual Basic type character.    iGetRecordNext%

v              Variable passed by value (local to a routine)
r              Variable passed by reference (local to a routine) 
Hungarian notation is as valuable in Visual Basic as it is in C. Although the Visual Basic type suffixes do indicate a variable's data type, they do not explain what a variable or function is used for, or how it can be accessed. Here are some examples: 
iSend - Represents a count of the number of messages sent
bSend - A Boolean flag defining the success of the last Send operation
hSend - A Handle to the Comm interface 
Each of these variable names tell a programmer something very different. This information is lost when the variable name is reduced to Send%. Scope prefixes such as g and m also help reduce the problem of name contention especially in multi-developer projects. 

Hungarian notation is also widely used by Windows C programmers and constantly referenced in Microsoft product documentation and in industry programming books. Additionally, the bond between C programmers and programmers who use Visual Basic will become much stronger as the Visual C++ development system gains momentum. This transition will result in many Visual Basic programmers moving to C for the first time and many programmers moving frequently back and forth between both environments. 
The Body of Variable and Routine Names
The body of a variable or routine name should use mixed case and should be as long as necessary to describe its purpose. In addition, function names should begin with a verb, such as InitNameArray or CloseDialog. 

For frequently used or long terms, standard abbreviations are recommended to help keep name lengths reasonable. In general, variable names greater than 32 characters can be difficult to read on VGA displays. 

When using abbreviations, make sure they are consistent throughout the entire application. Randomly switching between Cnt and Count within a project will lead to unnecessary confusion. 
Qualifiers on Variable and Routine Names
Related variables and routines are often used to manage and manipulate a common object. In these cases, use standard qualifiers to label the derivative variables and routines. Although putting the qualifier after the body of the name might seem a little awkward (as in sGetNameFirst, sGetNameLast instead of sGetFirstName, sGetLastName), this practice will help order these names together in the Visual Basic editor routine lists, making the logic and structure of the application easier to understand. The following table defines common qualifiers and their standard meaning: 
Qualifier  Description (follows Body)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
First      First element of a set.
Last       Last element of a set.
Next       Next element in a set.
Prev       Previous element in a set.
Cur        Current element in a set.
Min        Minimum value in a set.
Max        Maximum value in a set.
Save       Used to preserve another variable that must be reset later.
Tmp        A "scratch" variable whose scope is highly localized within the
           code. The value of a Tmp variable is usually only valid across
           a set of contiguous statements within a single procedure.
Src        Source. Frequently used in comparison and transfer routines.
Dst        Destination. Often used in conjunction with Source. 
User Defined Types
Declare user defined types in all caps with _TYPE appended to the end of the symbol name. For example: 
Type CUSTOMER_TYPE
      sName As String
      sState As String * 2
      lID as Long
   End Type 
When declaring an instance variable of a user defined type, add a prefix to the variable name to reference the type. For example: 
   Dim custNew as CUSTOMER_TYPE 
Naming Constants
The body of constant names should be UPPER_CASE with underscores (_) between words. Although standard Visual Basic constants do not include Hungarian information, prefixes like i, s, g, and m can be very useful in understanding the value and scope of a constant. For constant names, follow the same rules as variables. For Example: 
<mnUSER_LIST_MAX   ' Max entry limit for User list (integer value,
                     ' local to module)
   gsNEW_LINE        ' New Line character string (global to entire
                     ' application) 
Variant Data Type
If you know that a variable will always store data of a particular type, Visual Basic can handle that data more efficiently if you declare a variable of that type. 

However, the variant data type can be extremely useful when working with databases, messages, DDE, or OLE. Many databases allow NULL as a valid value for a field. Your code needs to distinguish between NULL, 0 (zero), and "" (empty string). Many times, these types of operations can use a generic service routine that does not need to know the type of data it receives to process or pass on the data. For example: 
   Sub ConvertNulls(rvntOrg As Variant, rvntSub As Variant)
      ' If rvntOrg = Null, replace the Null with rvntSub
      If IsNull(rvntOrg) Then rvntOrg = rvntSub
   End Sub 
The are some drawbacks, however, to using variants. Code statements that use variants can sometimes be ambiguous to the programmer. For example: 
   vnt1 = "10.01" : vnt2 = 11 : vnt3 = "11" : vnt4 = "x4"
   vntResult = vnt1 + vnt2  ' Does vntResult = 21.01 or 10.0111?
   vntResult = vnt2 + vnt1  ' Does vntResult = 21.01 or 1110.01?
   vntResult = vnt1 + vnt3  ' Does vntResult = 21.01 or 10.0111?
   vntResult = vnt3 + vnt1  ' Does vntResult = 21.01 or 1110.01?
   vntResult = vnt2 + vnt4  ' Does vntResult = 11x4 or ERROR?
   vntResult = vnt3 + vnt4  ' Does vntResult = 11x4 or ERROR? 
The above examples would be much less ambiguous and easier to read, debug, and maintain if the Visual Basic type conversion routines were used instead. For Example: 
   iVar1 = 5 + val(sVar2)   ' use this (explicit conversion)
   vntVar1 = 5 + vntVar2    ' not this (implicit conversion) 
Commenting Your Code
All procedures and functions should begin with a brief comment describing the functional characteristics of the routine (what it does). This description should not describe the implementation details (how it does it) because these often change over time, resulting in unnecessary comment maintenance work, or worse yet, erroneous comments. The code itself and any necessary in-line or local comments will describe the implementation. 

Parameters passed to a routine should be described when their functions are not obvious and when the routine expects the parameters to be in a specific range. Function return values and global variables that are changed by the routine (especially through reference parameters) must also be described at the beginning of each routine. 

Routine header comment blocks should look like this (see the next section "Formatting Your Code" for an example): 
Section    Comment Description
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose    What the routine does (not how).
Inputs     Each non-obvious parameter on a separate line with
           in-line comments
Assumes    List of each non-obvious external variable, control, open file,
           and so on.
Returns    Explanation of value returned for functions.
Effects    List of each effected external variable, control, file, and
           so on and the affect it has (only if this is not obvious) 
Every non-trivial variable declaration should include an in-line comment describing the use of the variable being declared. 

Variables, controls, and routines should be named clearly enough that in- line commenting is only needed for complex or non-intuitive implementation details. 

An overview description of the application, enumerating primary data objects, routines, algorithms, dialogs, database and file system dependencies, and so on should be included at the start of the .BAS module that contains the project's Visual Basic generic constant declarations. 

NOTE: The Project window inherently describes the list of files in a project, so this overview section only needs to provide information on the most important files and modules, or the files the Project window doesn't list, such as initialization (.INI) or database files. 
Formatting Your Code
Because many programmers still use VGA displays, screen real estate must be conserved as much as possible, while still allowing code formatting to reflect logic structure and nesting. 

Standard, tab-based, block nesting indentations should be two to four spaces. More than four spaces is unnecessary and can cause statements to be hidden or accidentally truncated. Less than two spaces does not sufficiently show logic nesting. In the Microsoft Knowledge Base, we use a three-space indent. Use the Environment Options dialog to set the default tab width. 

The functional overview comment of a routine should be indented one space. The highest level statements that follow the overview comment should be indented one tab, with each nested block indented an additional tab. For example: 
**************************************************************************
'Purpose:   Locate first occurrence of a specified user in UserList array.
'Inputs:    rasUserList():  the list of users to be searched
'           rsTargetUser:   the name of the user to search for
'Returns:   the index of the first occurrence of the rsTargetUser
'           in the rasUserList array. If target user not found, return -1.
'**************************************************************************

'VB3Line: Enter the following lines as one line
Function iFindUser (rasUserList() As String, rsTargetUser as String) _
   As Integer
   Dim i As Integer           ' loop counter
   Dim bFound As Integer      ' target found flag
   iFindUser = -1
   i = 0
   While i <= Ubound(rasUserList) and Not bFound
      If rasUserList(i) = rsTargetUser Then
         bFound = True
         iFindUser = i
      End If
   Wend
End Function 
Variables and non-generic constants should be grouped by function rather than by being split off into isolated areas or special files. Visual Basic generic constants such as HOURGLASS should be grouped in a single module (VB_STD.BAS) to keep them separate from application-specific declarations. 
Operators
Always use an ampersand (&) when concatenating strings, and use the plus sign (+) when working with numerical values. Using a plus sign (+) with non-numerical values, may cause problems when operating on two variants. For example: 
   vntVar1 = "10.01"
   vntVar2 = 11
   vntResult = vntVar1 + vntVar2         ' vntResult =  21.01
   vntResult = vntVar1 & vntVar2         ' vntResult = 10.0111 
Scope
Variables should always be defined with the smallest scope possible. Global variables can create enormously complex state machines and make the logic of an application extremely difficult to understand. Global variables also make the reuse and maintenance of your code much more difficult. Variables in Visual Basic can have the following scope: 
Scope             Variable Declared In:            Visibility
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Procedure-level   Event procedure, sub, or         Visible in the
                  function                         procedure in which
                                                   it is declared
Form-level,       Declarations section of a form   Visible in every
Module-level      or code module (.FRM, .BAS)      procedure in the
                                                   form or code
                                                   module
Global            Declarations section of a code   Always visible
                  module (.BAS, using Global
                  keyword) 
In a Visual Basic application, only use global variables when there is no other convenient way to share data between forms. You may want to consider storing information in a control's Tag property, which can be accessed globally using the form.object.property syntax. 

If you must use global variables, it is good practice to declare all of them in a single module and group them by function. Give the module a meaningful name that indicates its purpose, such as GLOBAL.BAS. 

With the exception of global variables (which should not be passed), procedures and functions should only operate on objects that are passed to them. Global variables that are used in routines should be identified in the general comment area at the beginning of the routine. In addition, pass arguments to subs and functions using ByVal, unless you explicitly want to change the value of the passed argument. 

Write modular code whenever possible. For example, if your application displays a dialog box, put all the controls and code required to perform the dialog's task in a single form. This helps to keep the application's code organized into useful components and minimizes its runtime overhead.

'This function gets an Item from the Database and adds it
'to the Collection. It returns the Item's position in the Collection.
Public Function AddItem(ByVal UserID As Variant) As Variant
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    Dim DALEng As IEBPPDAL.IEBPPDALEng
    Dim rsUsers As ADODB.Recordset
    Dim Errors As ADODB.Errors
    Dim User As CUser
            
    UserID = CleanString(UserID)
    If ValidateString(UserID) = True And ValidateUserID(UserID) = True Then
        'Build Parameter Array
        ReDim vParameters(0, 1)
        vParameters(0, 0) = VALUE_DB2USERID
        vParameters(0, 1) = "'" & UCase(UserID) & "'"
        'Query DAL
        If Not DALEng.ExecuteSP(SPNames.spBSUser_UserID, vParameters, GUID, rsUsers, SYSTEMIDCODE, Errors) Then
            'raise error
            Err.Raise USEREXECUTESPFAILED, "IEBPPUser.AddItem", "Call to ExecuteSP Failed with UserID. SPName was: SPNames.spBSUser_UserID"
            Exit Function
        End If
    Else
        'raise error
        Err.Raise USERPARMUSERIDNOTVALID, "IEBPPUser.AddItem", "UserID not valid on Parm check."
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    With User
        .UserPKID = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_USERSN)
        .UserID = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_USERID)
        .Password = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_PASSWORD)
        .ViolationCount = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_PASSWORD_VLTN)
        .Disabled = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_DISABLE_FLAG)
        .EmailAddress = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_EMAILADDR)
        .ChangePasswordFlag = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_PASSWORD_CHNGFLAG)
        .Timestamp = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_LAST_LOGON_TIMESTAMP)
        .EnrollCode = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_ACCT_ENRL_CD)
        .UserCodeWord = rsUsers.Fields(EBPPUSER_CD_WRD)
        .Dirty = False 'Remember initial load nothing is dirty
        Set .Parent = Me
        .Loaded = True
    End With
    
    AddItem = Me.Count
    Exit Function

    Dim ErrDescription As String

'This method is used to Add a new User to the collection. This method is
'disabled (using an internal check) when NewUserMode = True.
'It will return 0 if it doesn't work or else it will return the
'position of the Item that was added.

Public Function Add(ByVal UserID As Variant, ByVal Password As Variant, ByVal EmailAddress As Variant) As Variant
    Dim oCUser As CUser
    Dim lngPKID As Long
    Dim Sec As IEBPPSecurityEng
    Dim Session As IEBPPSecurity.colSession
    Dim Role As eEBPPSecurityRole
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    
    'Do this first because we might not have a GUID
    If NewUserMode = True Then
        'raise error
        Err.Raise USERNEWUSERMODESET, "colUser.Add", "Function not supported when NewUserMode set."
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    Add = 0
    'Check Business Conditions
    '(if appropriate -- Remember that the properties will check their own)
    
    'CSR Only
    Set Sec = New IEBPPSecurityEng
    
    If Sec.VerifyLogin(Me.GUID) <> eVerifyLoginSuccess Then
        'Raise Error
        Err.Raise USERSECURITYFAILED, "colUser.Add", "Security Check Failed for GUID: " & GUID
        Exit Function
    End If
    Set Session = Sec.GetSession(GUID)
    Set Sec = Nothing
    Role = Session.Item(1).Role
    
    If Role = eEBPPCustomer Then
        Err.Raise USERSECURITYFAILED, "colUser.Add", "User is not in corect role"
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    If ValidateString(UserID) = False Then
        'raise error
        Err.Raise USERPARMUSERIDNOTVALID, "colUser.Add", "UserID passed in was invalid."
        Exit Function
    End If
    If ValidateString(Password) = False Then
        'raise error
        Err.Raise USERPARMPASSWORDNOTVALID, "colUser.Add", "Password passed in was invalid."
        Exit Function
    End If
    If ValidateString(EmailAddress) = False Then
        'raise error
        Err.Raise USERPARMEMAILADDRESSNOTVALID, "colUser.Add", "EmailAddress passed in was invalid."
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    Set oCUser = New CUser
    With oCUser
        .UserPKID = 0
        .UserID = UserID
        .Password = Password
        .ViolationCount = 0
        .Disabled = False
        .EmailAddress = EmailAddress
        .ChangePasswordFlag = False
        .Timestamp = Now()
        .Dirty = True
        .EnrollCode = ""
        .UserCodeWord = ""
        Set .Parent = Me
    End With
    
    If mcolStorage Is Nothing Then
        Set mcolStorage = New Collection
    End If

    mcolStorage.Add oCUser, UserID 'assume that we never use Before or After.
    Add = mcolStorage.Count
    
    Set oCUser = Nothing
'generated Exit Code
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
'Code to try and handle the Error

'If not Handled then Raise the Error
    Dim ErrNumber As Long
    Dim ErrSource As String
    Dim ErrDescription As String

    ErrNumber = Err.Number
    ErrSource = Err.Source
    ErrDescription = Err.Description

    Set oCUser = Nothing
    
    Call RaiseError(ErrNumber, ErrSource, "colUser.Add", ErrDescription)
    Exit Function

'This method is used to write the information in the collection to the DB.
'This method should have a conditional check to see if one and only one user
'is being written to the DB when NewUserMode = True.
'
Private Function DoUpdate(Optional ByVal IndexKey As Variant, Optional UpdateFlag As Boolean = True) As Variant
    Dim SysParmEng As IEBPPSystemEng
    Dim oCSysParm As CSystemParm
    Dim Sec As IEBPPSecurityEng
    Dim Session As IEBPPSecurity.colSession
    Dim SecRetVal As eEBPPVerifyLoginReturn
    Dim ErrNum As Long
    Dim Role As eEBPPSecurityRole
    Dim DALEng As IEBPPDAL.IEBPPDALEng
    Dim rsUsers As ADODB.Recordset
    Dim Errors As ADODB.Errors
    Dim vParameters() As Variant
    Dim LowerLimit As Long
    Dim UpperLimit As Long
    Dim inx As Long
    Dim IsUpdate As Boolean
    Dim lngPKID As Long
    Dim oCUser As CUser
    Dim spNum As SPNames
    Dim vReturnParms As Variant
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    
    DoUpdate = False
    
    'Check the Parm passed in
    If Not IsMissing(IndexKey) Then
        If Not IsNumeric(IndexKey) And Not IsEmpty(IndexKey) Then
            'raise error
            Err.Raise USERINVALIDDATATYPE, "colUser.Update", "Invalid IndexKey passed in. Not Numeric."
            Exit Function
        End If
        If IndexKey <= 0 Or IndexKey > Me.Count Then
            'raise error
            Err.Raise USERINVALIDDATATYPE, "colUser.Update", "Invalid IndexKey passed in. Out of Range"
            Exit Function
        End If
    End If
'**************Updating Normal User Information******************
' A Customer or CSR Updating or Inserting a new user and we have to persist the data
    
    'check security
    If Not SafeCreateObject(Sec, OBJ_SECURITYENG, ErrNum) Then
        'Raise error
        Err.Raise SAFECREATEFAILED_ERR, "colUser.Update", "Failed to Create: " & OBJ_SECURITYENG & vbCrLf & "Return Code was " & ErrNum
    End If

    SecRetVal = Sec.VerifyLogin(Me.GUID)
    If SecRetVal <> eVerifyLoginSuccess Then
        'Raise Error
        Err.Raise USERSECURITYFAILED, "colUser.Update", "Security Check Failed for GUID: " & GUID
        Exit Function
    End If
    '
    ' Get the role from the session item
    Set Session = Sec.GetSession(GUID)
    Role = Session.Item(1).Role
    '
    Set Sec = Nothing
    
    'Everything is ok so Update the DB
    'Create DAL
    If UpdateFlag Then    'Don't create DAL if not actually updating
        If Not SafeCreateObject(DALEng, OBJ_DALENG, ErrNum) Then
            'Raise error
            Err.Raise SAFECREATEFAILED_ERR, "colUser.Update", "Failed to Create: " & OBJ_DALENG & vbCrLf & "Return Code was " & ErrNum
        End If
    End If

    'If Customer then we only want to update one Record
    If Role = eEBPPCustomer Then
        If Me.Count = 1 Then
            'Customer can't update everything
            LowerLimit = IIf(IsMissing(IndexKey), 1, IndexKey)
            UpperLimit = IIf(IsMissing(IndexKey), Me.Count, IndexKey)
            For inx = LowerLimit To UpperLimit
                Set oCUser = Me.Item(inx)
                If oCUser.Dirty Then
                    
                    ' Then we want to update this in the DB
                    ReDim vParameters(7, 1)              'Dimension the param array based on the constant stored in the constants module
                    vParameters(0, 0) = VALUE_DB2USERPKID      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                    vParameters(0, 1) = oCUser.UserPKID 'Now fill in the value
                    vParameters(1, 0) = VALUE_DB2USERID      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                    vParameters(1, 1) = "'" & oCUser.UserID & "'" 'Now fill in the value
                    vParameters(2, 0) = VALUE_DB2PASSWORD      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                    vParameters(2, 1) = "'" & oCUser.Password & "'" 'Now fill in the value
                    vParameters(3, 0) = VALUE_DB2EMAIL      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                    vParameters(3, 1) = "'" & oCUser.EmailAddress & "'" 'Now fill in the value
                    vParameters(4, 0) = VALUE_DB2CHANGEPWD      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                    vParameters(4, 1) = "'" & oCUser.StorageChangePasswordFlag & "'" 'Now fill in the value
                    vParameters(5, 0) = VALUE_DB2LASTLOGON      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                    vParameters(5, 1) = "'" & Format(Now(), MAINFRAMETIMESTAMPFORMAT) & "'" 'Now fill in the value
                    vParameters(6, 0) = VALUE_DB2ACCTENRLCD
                    vParameters(6, 1) = oCUser.EnrollCodeFK
                    vParameters(7, 0) = VALUE_DB2USRCDWRD
                    vParameters(7, 1) = "'" & oCUser.UserCodeWord & "'"
                    
                    If Not UpdateFlag Then
                        'package up the parms
                        If IsEmpty(vReturnParms) Then
                            ReDim vReturnParms(1, 0)
                        Else
                            ReDim Preserve vReturnParms(1, UBound(vReturnParms, 2) + 1)
                        End If
                        vReturnParms(0, inx - 1) = SPNames.spBUUser_Cust
                        vReturnParms(1, inx - 1) = vParameters
                    Else
                        'Call Update SP
                        If Not DALEng.ExecuteSP(SPNames.spBUUser_Cust, vParameters, Me.GUID, rsUsers, SYSTEMIDCODE, Errors) Then
                            'raise error
                            Err.Raise USEREXECUTESPFAILED, "colUser.Update", "Call to ExecuteSP. SPName was: SPNames.spBUUser_Cust"
                            Exit Function
                        End If
                    End If
                End If
                Set oCUser = Nothing
            Next
        Else
            'raise error
            Err.Raise USERTOOMANYITEMS, "colUser.Update", "Function not supported. Too many Items: " & Me.Count & " Security Return Value: " & SecRetVal
            Exit Function
        End If
    End If 'Customer
    
    If Role = eEBPPCSR Or Role = eEBPPCBR Then
        'CSR can update everything
        LowerLimit = IIf(IsMissing(IndexKey), 1, IndexKey)
        UpperLimit = IIf(IsMissing(IndexKey), Me.Count, IndexKey)
        For inx = LowerLimit To UpperLimit
            Set oCUser = Me.Item(inx)
            IsUpdate = True  'means Do an Update
            
            If oCUser.Dirty Then
                ' Then we want to update this in the DB, let's check if it's a new one.
                ReDim vParameters(9, 1)              'Dimension the param array based on the constant stored in the constants module
                vParameters(0, 0) = VALUE_DB2USERPKID      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                If oCUser.UserPKID = 0 Then
                        'Generate PKID
                        lngPKID = GetPKID()
                        If lngPKID = 0 Then
                            'raise error
                            Err.Raise USERPRIMARYKEYNOTVALID, "colUser.Update", "Primary Key was invalid. Could not be created."
                            Exit Function
                        Else
                            IsUpdate = False    'Means Do an Insert
                            oCUser.UserPKID = lngPKID
                        End If
                End If
                vParameters(0, 1) = oCUser.UserPKID 'Now fill in the value
                vParameters(1, 0) = VALUE_DB2USERID      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                vParameters(1, 1) = "'" & oCUser.UserID & "'" 'Now fill in the value
                vParameters(2, 0) = VALUE_DB2PASSWORD      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                vParameters(2, 1) = "'" & oCUser.Password & "'" 'Now fill in the value
                vParameters(3, 0) = VALUE_DB2VIOLATIONCNT      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                vParameters(3, 1) = oCUser.ViolationCount 'Now fill in the value
                vParameters(4, 0) = VALUE_DB2DISALBED      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                vParameters(4, 1) = "'" & oCUser.StorageDisabled & "'" 'Now fill in the value
                vParameters(5, 0) = VALUE_DB2EMAIL      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                vParameters(5, 1) = "'" & oCUser.EmailAddress & "'" 'Now fill in the value
                vParameters(6, 0) = VALUE_DB2CHANGEPWD      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                vParameters(6, 1) = "'" & oCUser.StorageChangePasswordFlag & "'" 'Now fill in the value
                vParameters(7, 0) = VALUE_DB2LASTLOGON      'This will equal the parameter to replace in the stored procedure, ie: &@UserName
                vParameters(7, 1) = "'" & Format(Now(), MAINFRAMETIMESTAMPFORMAT) & "'" 'Now fill in the value
                vParameters(8, 0) = VALUE_DB2ACCTENRLCD
                vParameters(8, 1) = oCUser.EnrollCodeFK
                vParameters(9, 0) = VALUE_DB2USRCDWRD
                vParameters(9, 1) = "'" & oCUser.UserCodeWord & "'"
                'Check to see if we should do an Update or Insert SP
                If IsUpdate = True Then
                    spNum = SPNames.spUUser
                Else
                    spNum = SPNames.spIUser
                End If
                If Not UpdateFlag Then
                    'package up the parms
                    If IsEmpty(vReturnParms) Then
                        ReDim vReturnParms(1, 0)
                    Else
                        ReDim Preserve vReturnParms(1, UBound(vReturnParms, 2) + 1)
                    End If
                    vReturnParms(0, inx - 1) = spNum
                    vReturnParms(1, inx - 1) = vParameters
                Else
                    'Call Update or Insert SP
                    If Not DALEng.ExecuteSP(spNum, vParameters, Me.GUID, rsUsers, SYSTEMIDCODE, Errors) Then
                       'raise error
                       Err.Raise USEREXECUTESPFAILED, "colUser.Update", "Call to ExecuteSP. SPName was: SPNames.spUUser"
                       Exit Function
                    End If
                End If
              End If
            Set oCUser = Nothing
        Next
    End If 'CSR
    
    Set DALEng = Nothing
    Set rsUsers = Nothing
    Set Errors = Nothing
    Set oCUser = Nothing
    
    If UpdateFlag Then
        DoUpdate = True
    Else
        DoUpdate = vReturnParms
    End If
'generated Exit Code
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
'Code to try and handle the Error

'If not Handled then Raise the Error
    Dim ErrNumber As Long
    Dim ErrSource As String
    Dim ErrDescription As String

    ErrNumber = Err.Number
    ErrSource = Err.Source
    ErrDescription = Err.Description

    Set SysParmEng = Nothing
    Set oCSysParm = Nothing

    Set oCUser = Nothing
