'This method deletes an item from the DB. A check needs to be done to make sure
'that the User is a CSR.
Private Function DoDelete(ByVal IndexKey As Variant, Optional ByVal UpdateFlag As Boolean = True) As Variant
    Dim Sec As IEBPPSecurityEng
    Dim DALEng As IEBPPDALEng
    Dim rsUsers As ADODB.Recordset
    Dim Errors As ADODB.Errors
    Dim vParameters() As Variant
    Dim Session As IEBPPSecurity.colSession
    Dim vReturnParms As Variant
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
        'Do this first because we might not have a GUID
        If NewUserMode = True Then
            'raise error
            Err.Raise USERNEWUSERMODESET, "colUsers.Delete", "Function not supported when NewUserMode set."
            Exit Function
        End If
        
        DoDelete = False
        
        'Check Security to see if GUID valid and the Role is CSR
        Set Sec = New IEBPPSecurityEng
        If Sec.VerifyLogin(Me.GUID) <> eVerifyLoginSuccess Then
            'Raise Error
            Err.Raise USERSECURITYFAILED, "colUser.Delete", "Security Check Failed for GUID: " & GUID
            Exit Function
        End If
        Set Session = Sec.GetSession(GUID)
        If Session.Item(1).Role = eEBPPCustomer Then
            Err.Raise USERSECURITYFAILED, "colUser.Delete", "Security Check Failed for GUID: " & GUID
            Exit Function
        End If
        Set Sec = Nothing
        Set Session = Nothing
        'We know the GUID is valid and Role is not customer
        'Set DALEng = New IEBPPDALEng
        'Set rsUsers = New Recordset
        
        'Build Parameter Array
        ReDim vParameters(0, 1)
        vParameters(0, 0) = VALUE_DB2USERPKID
        vParameters(0, 1) = Me.Item(IndexKey).UserPKID
        If Not UpdateFlag Then
            ReDim vReturnParms(1, 0)
            vReturnParms(0, 0) = SPNames.spDUser
            vReturnParms(1, 0) = vParameters
            DoDelete = vReturnParms
            Exit Function
        End If
        If Not SafeCreateObject(DALEng, OBJ_DALENG, Error) Then
            Err.Raise SAFECREATEFAILED_ERR, "colUser.DoDelete", "Unable to create Data Access Object"
            Exit Function
        End If
        'Query DAL
        If Not DALEng.ExecuteSP(SPNames.spDUser, vParameters, Me.GUID, rsUsers, SYSTEMIDCODE, Errors) Then
            Err.Raise USEREXECUTESPFAILED, "colUser.Delete", "Call to ExecuteSP Failed. SPName was: SPNames.spDUser"
            Exit Function
        End If
        
        Set rsUsers = Nothing
        Set DALEng = Nothing
        Set Sec = Nothing
        DoDelete = True
        
'generated Exit Code
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
'Code to try and handle the Error

'If not Handled then Raise the Error
    Dim ErrNumber As Long
    Dim ErrSource As String
    Dim ErrDescription As String
    
    Set Session = Nothing
    Set DALEng = Nothing
    Set rsUsers = Nothing
    ErrNumber = Err.Number
    ErrSource = Err.Source
    ErrDescription = Err.Description

    Call RaiseError(ErrNumber, ErrSource, "colUser.Delete", ErrDescription)
    Exit Function
End Function

Public Function SafeCreateObject(Target As Object, ByVal ClassName As String, Optional ErrorNumber As Long) As Boolean

    Dim ctxObj As COMSVCSLib.ObjectContext

    On Error Resume Next
    
    Set ctxObj = GetObjectContext()
    
    'Use existing context if it exists
    If Not ctxObj Is Nothing Then
        Set Target = ctxObj.CreateInstance(ClassName)
    Else
        Set Target = CreateObject(ClassName)
    End If
    
    If Err <> 0 Then
        ErrorNumber = Err.Number
        SafeCreateObject = False
    Else
        ErrorNumber = 0
        SafeCreateObject = True
    End If
    
    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "SafeCreateObject '" & ClassName & "' Created: " & SafeCreateObject)
    #End If
    
    Err.Clear
    
    Exit Function
    
End Function

' ==========================================================================================
' Name              modErrorHandling - HandleException
'
' Parameters
'       SecurityToken           (I) Variant
'       ErrorNumber             (I) long
'       ErrorDescription        (I) string
'       LineNumber              (I) long = 0
'       ErrorSource             (I) string
'       CancelError             (I) boolean = false
'       OriginalSource          (I) string
'
' Returns
'      boolean
'
' Synopsis:
'
'
' Design Details:
'
'
' ==========================================================================================
Public Function HandleException(ByVal SecurityToken As Variant, ByVal ErrorNumber As Long, ByVal ErrorDescription As String, Optional ByVal LineNumber As Long = 0, Optional ByVal ErrorSource As String, Optional CancelError As Boolean = False, Optional OriginalSource As String)
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler

    Dim strUserMsg As String
    Dim strVer As String
    Dim lngUnMaskedErrorNumber As Long
    Dim errNum As Long

    #If DebugVersion Then
        Dim strMsg As String
        strMsg = DebugPrefix & "Entering HandleException"
        strMsg = strMsg & vbCrLf & "   Error Number = " & ErrorNumber & " (Hex = " & Hex(ErrorNumber) & ")"
        strMsg = strMsg & vbCrLf & "   Error Description = " & ErrorDescription
        strMsg = strMsg & vbCrLf & "   Error Line Number = " & LineNumber
        strMsg = strMsg & vbCrLf & "   Error Source = " & ErrorSource
        strMsg = strMsg & vbCrLf & "   Error Original Source = " & OriginalSource
        Call OutputDebugString(strMsg)
    #End If

    'Add version information to string
    strVer = "(Version " & App.Major & "." & App.Minor & "." & App.Revision
    If InStr(ErrorSource, "(Version") = 0 Then
        If Not IsMissing(LineNumber) Then
            strVer = strVer & ", Line " & LineNumber
        End If
        ErrorSource = Trim(ErrorSource) & "  " & strVer & ")"
    End If

    strUserMsg = ""
    
    'Not our Components
    If (ErrorNumber And %%Application Name%%ExApplicationResult) <> %%Application Name%%ExApplicationResult Then
        'If no one else has logged it and is not a business rule, then we will
        If (ErrorNumber And %%Application Name%%ExExceptionLogged) <> %%Application Name%%ExExceptionLogged Then
            'Send a Message to the log
            If Not LogError(ErrorNumber, ErrorSource, "(EXTERNAL COMPONENT)" & ErrorDescription) Then
                'raise error
                On Error GoTo 0
                Err.Raise ERR_LOGERRORFAILED, "modErrorHandler.HandleException", "The call to LogError failed for external components."
            End If
            'Mark ErrorNumber as Logged
            ErrorNumber = (ErrorNumber Or OBPExExceptionLogged)
        End If
    Else
    'One of our Components
                
        'Unmask the Error number to get the value
        If (ErrorNumber And %%Application Name%%ExBusinessRule) = %%Application Name%%ExBusinessRule Then
            lngUnMaskedErrorNumber = (ErrorNumber And ErrorMask)
        Else
            lngUnMaskedErrorNumber = (ErrorNumber And ErrorMask) - %%Application Name%%ExBusinessRule
        End If
    
        'Retrieve the user text message
        strUserMsg = GetErrorText(lngUnMaskedErrorNumber)
        
        If ((ErrorNumber And %%Application Name%%ExExceptionLogged) <> %%Application Name%%ExExceptionLogged) And ((ErrorNumber And %%Application Name%%ExBusinessRule) <> %%Application Name%%ExBusinessRule) Then
            'Send a Message to the log
            If Not LogError(ErrorNumber, ErrorSource, "INTERNAL COMPONENT: (Dec:" & lngUnMaskedErrorNumber & ": Hex:" & Hex(ErrorNumber) & ")" & vbCrLf & strUserMsg & vbCrLf & ErrorDescription) Then
                'raise error
                On Error GoTo 0
                Err.Raise ERR_LOGERRORFAILED, "modErrorHandler.RaiseError", "The call to LogError failed for our components."
            End If

            'Mark ErrorNumber as Logged
            ErrorNumber = (ErrorNumber Or %%Application Name%%ExExceptionLogged)
        End If
    End If

    'Pass it up the stream
    If Not CancelError Then
        On Error GoTo 0
        Err.Raise ErrorNumber, ErrorSource, IIf(strUserMsg = "", ErrorDescription, strUserMsg)
    End If
    
CleanExit:
    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(vbCrLf & "Leaving HandleException - success")
    #End If
    'generated Exit Code
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
'Code to try and handle the Error

'If not Handled then Raise the Error
    Dim ErrNumber As Long
    Dim errSource As String
    Dim ErrDescription As String

    ErrNumber = Err.Number
    errSource = Err.Source
    ErrDescription = Err.Description
        
    Call Err.Raise(ErrNumber, errSource, "%%Application Name%%: modErrorHandling.HandleException" & vbCrLf & ErrDescription)
    Exit Function
    
End Function

' ==========================================================================================
' Name              modErrorHandling - LogError
'
' Parameters
'       ErrorNumber             (I) long
'       ErrorSource             (I) string
'       ErrorDescription        (I) string
'
' Returns
'      boolean
'
' Synopsis:
'   This function is used to write out an Error Log entry to either the NT Event
'   Viewer or a DB table.  If writing to the NTEvent Log then the NT Event type
'   should always be:
'           vbLogEventTypeError     1     Error
'
' Design Details:
'
'
' ==========================================================================================

Private Function LogError(ByVal ErrorNumber As Long, ByVal ErrorSource As String, ByVal ErrorDescription As String) As Boolean
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    
    Dim strMessage As String
    Dim strSourceName As String
    Dim strServerName As String
    Dim strLogging As String
    Dim bEnabled As Boolean
    Dim iLogType As LogEventTypeConstants
    
    LogError = False
    
    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "Entering modErrorHandling.LogError")
    #End If
    
    ' My Computer\HKCU\Software\VB and VBA Program Settings\
    strServerName = GetSetting(APPLICATIONNAME, "Log", "MachineName")
    strLogging = GetSetting(APPLICATIONNAME, "Log", "Enabled")
    
    If strLogging = "" Then
        Call SaveSetting(APPLICATIONNAME, "Log", "Enabled", DEFAULTLOGMODE)
    End If
    
    If UCase(strLogging) = "TRUE" Then
        bEnabled = True
    Else
        GoTo CleanExit
    End If
    
    strSourceName = APPLICATIONNAME
    
    If strServerName = "" Then
        Call SaveSetting(APPLICATIONNAME, "Log", "MachineName", DEFAULTSERVERNAME)
    End If
   
    'Make the Error Message Readable
    strMessage = vbCrLf & "Number: " & ErrorNumber & " (Hex = " & Hex(ErrorNumber) & ")" & vbCrLf & "Source: " & ErrorSource & vbCrLf & "Description: " & ErrorDescription & vbCrLf
    
    'Determine type
    If (ErrorNumber And %%Application Name%%ExApplicationResult) <> %%Application Name%%ExApplicationResult Then
        iLogType = vbLogEventTypeError
        ErrorNumber = DEFAULTAPPEVENTID
    ElseIf ((ErrorNumber And %%Application Name%%ExBusinessRule) <> %%Application Name%%ExBusinessRule) Then
        iLogType = vbLogEventTypeError
    Else
        iLogType = vbLogEventTypeWarning
    End If
     
    'Write to NT EventViewer
    'This call will pass the Error Number as the EventID. This is useful if the
    'Error is from one of our components as it will be the Unmasked Error number.
    If strServerName = "" Or strServerName = DEFAULTSERVERNAME Then
        Call LogNTEvent(strMessage, , strSourceName, iLogType, ErrorNumber)
    Else
        Call LogNTEvent(strMessage, strServerName, strSourceName, iLogType, ErrorNumber)
    End If
    
CleanExit:
    LogError = True
    
    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "Leaving modErrorHandling.LogError - SUCCESS")
    #End If
    
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
'Code to try and handle the Error

'If not Handled then Raise the Error
    Dim ErrNumber As Long
    Dim errSource As String
    Dim ErrDescription As String

    ErrNumber = Err.Number
    errSource = Err.Source
    ErrDescription = Err.Description
    
    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "Leaving modErrorHandling.LogError - FAILURE")
    #End If
    
    Call Err.Raise(ErrNumber, errSource, "modErrorHandling.LogError" & ErrDescription)
    Exit Function
    
End Function

    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "Entering modErrorHandling.LogNTEvent")

    If IsMissing(sServerName) Then
        sServerName = vbNullString
    ElseIf Trim(sServerName) = "" Then

    End If

INFO: Microsoft Consulting Services Naming Conventions for Visual Basic

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The information in this article applies to:

Microsoft Visual Basic Standard, Professional, and Enterprise Editions, 16-bit and 32-bit, for Windows, version 4.0 
Microsoft Visual Basic Standard and Professional Editions for Windows, versions 2.0, 3.0

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


SUMMARY
It is a good idea to establish naming conventions for your Visual Basic code. This article gives you the naming conventions used by Microsoft Consulting Services (MCS). 

This document is a superset of the Visual Basic coding conventions found in the Visual Basic "Programmer's Guide." 

NOTE: The third-party controls mentioned in this article are manufactured by vendors independent of Microsoft. Microsoft makes no warranty, implied or otherwise, regarding these controls' performance or reliability. 

MORE INFORMATION
Naming conventions help Visual Basic programmers: 

	- standardize the structure, coding style and logic of an application.
	- create precise, readable, and unambiguous source code.
	- be consistent with other language conventions (most importantly, the Visual Basic Programmers Guide and standard Windows C Hungarian notation).
	- be efficient from a string size and labor standpoint, thus allowing a greater opportunity for longer and fuller object names.
	- define the minimal requirements necessary to do the above. 

Setting Environment Options
Use Option Explicit. Declare all variables to save programming time by reducing the number of bugs caused by typos (for example, aUserNameTmp vs. sUserNameTmp vs. sUserNameTemp). In the Environment Options dialog, set Require Variable Declaration to Yes. The Option Explicit statement requires you to declare all the variables in your Visual Basic program. Save Files as ASCII Text. Save form (.FRM) and module (.BAS) files as ASCII text to facilitate the use of version control systems and minimize the damage that can be caused by disk corruption. In addition, you can: 

	- use your own editor
	- use automated tools, such as grep
	- create code generation or CASE tools for Visual Basic
	- perform external analysis of your Visual Basic code

Hungarian notation is as valuable in Visual Basic as it is in C. Although the Visual Basic type suffixes do indicate a variable's data type, they do not explain what a variable or function is used for, or how it can be accessed. Here are some examples: 
iSend - Represents a count of the number of messages sent
bSend - A Boolean flag defining the success of the last Send operation
hSend - A Handle to the Comm interface 
Each of these variable names tell a programmer something very different. This information is lost when the variable name is reduced to Send%. Scope prefixes such as g and m also help reduce the problem of name contention especially in multi-developer projects. 

Hungarian notation is also widely used by Windows C programmers and constantly referenced in Microsoft product documentation and in industry programming books. Additionally, the bond between C programmers and programmers who use Visual Basic will become much stronger as the Visual C++ development system gains momentum. This transition will result in many Visual Basic programmers moving to C for the first time and many programmers moving frequently back and forth between both environments. 
The Body of Variable and Routine Names
The body of a variable or routine name should use mixed case and should be as long as necessary to describe its purpose. In addition, function names should begin with a verb, such as InitNameArray or CloseDialog. 

For frequently used or long terms, standard abbreviations are recommended to help keep name lengths reasonable. In general, variable names greater than 32 characters can be difficult to read on VGA displays. 

When using abbreviations, make sure they are consistent throughout the entire application. Randomly switching between Cnt and Count within a project will lead to unnecessary confusion. 
Qualifiers on Variable and Routine Names
Related variables and routines are often used to manage and manipulate a common object. In these cases, use standard qualifiers to label the derivative variables and routines. Although putting the qualifier after the body of the name might seem a little awkward (as in sGetNameFirst, sGetNameLast instead of sGetFirstName, sGetLastName), this practice will help order these names together in the Visual Basic editor routine lists, making the logic and structure of the application easier to understand. The following table defines common qualifiers and their standard meaning: 
Qualifier  Description (follows Body)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
First      First element of a set.
Last       Last element of a set.
Next       Next element in a set.
Prev       Previous element in a set.
Cur        Current element in a set.
Min        Minimum value in a set.
Max        Maximum value in a set.
Save       Used to preserve another variable that must be reset later.
Tmp        A "scratch" variable whose scope is highly localized within the
           code. The value of a Tmp variable is usually only valid across
           a set of contiguous statements within a single procedure.
Src        Source. Frequently used in comparison and transfer routines.
Dst        Destination. Often used in conjunction with Source. 
User Defined Types
Declare user defined types in all caps with _TYPE appended to the end of the symbol name. For example: 
Type CUSTOMER_TYPE
      sName As String
      sState As String * 2
      lID as Long
   End Type 
When declaring an instance variable of a user defined type, add a prefix to the variable name to reference the type. For example: 
   Dim custNew as CUSTOMER_TYPE 
Naming Constants
The body of constant names should be UPPER_CASE with underscores (_) between words. Although standard Visual Basic constants do not include Hungarian information, prefixes like i, s, g, and m can be very useful in understanding the value and scope of a constant. For constant names, follow the same rules as variables. For Example: 
<mnUSER_LIST_MAX   ' Max entry limit for User list (integer value,
                     ' local to module)
   gsNEW_LINE        ' New Line character string (global to entire
                     ' application) 
Variant Data Type
If you know that a variable will always store data of a particular type, Visual Basic can handle that data more efficiently if you declare a variable of that type. 

However, the variant data type can be extremely useful when working with databases, messages, DDE, or OLE. Many databases allow NULL as a valid value for a field. Your code needs to distinguish between NULL, 0 (zero), and "" (empty string). Many times, these types of operations can use a generic service routine that does not need to know the type of data it receives to process or pass on the data. For example: 
   Sub ConvertNulls(rvntOrg As Variant, rvntSub As Variant)
      ' If rvntOrg = Null, replace the Null with rvntSub
      If IsNull(rvntOrg) Then rvntOrg = rvntSub
   End Sub 
The are some drawbacks, however, to using variants. Code statements that use variants can sometimes be ambiguous to the programmer. For example: 
   vnt1 = "10.01" : vnt2 = 11 : vnt3 = "11" : vnt4 = "x4"
   vntResult = vnt1 + vnt2  ' Does vntResult = 21.01 or 10.0111?
   vntResult = vnt2 + vnt1  ' Does vntResult = 21.01 or 1110.01?
   vntResult = vnt1 + vnt3  ' Does vntResult = 21.01 or 10.0111?
   vntResult = vnt3 + vnt1  ' Does vntResult = 21.01 or 1110.01?
   vntResult = vnt2 + vnt4  ' Does vntResult = 11x4 or ERROR?
   vntResult = vnt3 + vnt4  ' Does vntResult = 11x4 or ERROR? 
The above examples would be much less ambiguous and easier to read, debug, and maintain if the Visual Basic type conversion routines were used instead. For Example: 
   iVar1 = 5 + val(sVar2)   ' use this (explicit conversion)
   vntVar1 = 5 + vntVar2    ' not this (implicit conversion) 
Commenting Your Code
All procedures and functions should begin with a brief comment describing the functional characteristics of the routine (what it does). This description should not describe the implementation details (how it does it) because these often change over time, resulting in unnecessary comment maintenance work, or worse yet, erroneous comments. The code itself and any necessary in-line or local comments will describe the implementation. 

Parameters passed to a routine should be described when their functions are not obvious and when the routine expects the parameters to be in a specific range. Function return values and global variables that are changed by the routine (especially through reference parameters) must also be described at the beginning of each routine. 

Routine header comment blocks should look like this (see the next section "Formatting Your Code" for an example): 
Section    Comment Description
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Purpose    What the routine does (not how).
Inputs     Each non-obvious parameter on a separate line with
           in-line comments
Assumes    List of each non-obvious external variable, control, open file,
           and so on.
Returns    Explanation of value returned for functions.
Effects    List of each effected external variable, control, file, and
           so on and the affect it has (only if this is not obvious) 
Every non-trivial variable declaration should include an in-line comment describing the use of the variable being declared. 

Variables, controls, and routines should be named clearly enough that in- line commenting is only needed for complex or non-intuitive implementation details. 

An overview description of the application, enumerating primary data objects, routines, algorithms, dialogs, database and file system dependencies, and so on should be included at the start of the .BAS module that contains the project's Visual Basic generic constant declarations. 

NOTE: The Project window inherently describes the list of files in a project, so this overview section only needs to provide information on the most important files and modules, or the files the Project window doesn't list, such as initialization (.INI) or database files. 
Formatting Your Code
Because many programmers still use VGA displays, screen real estate must be conserved as much as possible, while still allowing code formatting to reflect logic structure and nesting. 

Standard, tab-based, block nesting indentations should be two to four spaces. More than four spaces is unnecessary and can cause statements to be hidden or accidentally truncated. Less than two spaces does not sufficiently show logic nesting. In the Microsoft Knowledge Base, we use a three-space indent. Use the Environment Options dialog to set the default tab width. 

The functional overview comment of a routine should be indented one space. The highest level statements that follow the overview comment should be indented one tab, with each nested block indented an additional tab. For example: 
**************************************************************************
'Purpose:   Locate first occurrence of a specified user in UserList array.
'Inputs:    rasUserList():  the list of users to be searched
'           rsTargetUser:   the name of the user to search for
'Returns:   the index of the first occurrence of the rsTargetUser
'           in the rasUserList array. If target user not found, return -1.
'**************************************************************************

'VB3Line: Enter the following lines as one line
Function iFindUser (rasUserList() As String, rsTargetUser as String) _
   As Integer
   Dim i As Integer           ' loop counter
   Dim bFound As Integer      ' target found flag
   iFindUser = -1
   i = 0
   While i <= Ubound(rasUserList) and Not bFound
      If rasUserList(i) = rsTargetUser Then
         bFound = True
         iFindUser = i
      End If
   Wend
End Function 
Variables and non-generic constants should be grouped by function rather than by being split off into isolated areas or special files. Visual Basic generic constants such as HOURGLASS should be grouped in a single module (VB_STD.BAS) to keep them separate from application-specific declarations. 
Operators
Always use an ampersand (&) when concatenating strings, and use the plus sign (+) when working with numerical values. Using a plus sign (+) with non-numerical values, may cause problems when operating on two variants. For example: 
   vntVar1 = "10.01"
   vntVar2 = 11
   vntResult = vntVar1 + vntVar2         ' vntResult =  21.01
   vntResult = vntVar1 & vntVar2         ' vntResult = 10.0111 
Scope
Variables should always be defined with the smallest scope possible. Global variables can create enormously complex state machines and make the logic of an application extremely difficult to understand. Global variables also make the reuse and maintenance of your code much more difficult. Variables in Visual Basic can have the following scope: 
Scope             Variable Declared In:            Visibility
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Procedure-level   Event procedure, sub, or         Visible in the
                  function                         procedure in which
                                                   it is declared
Form-level,       Declarations section of a form   Visible in every
Module-level      or code module (.FRM, .BAS)      procedure in the
                                                   form or code
                                                   module
Global            Declarations section of a code   Always visible
                  module (.BAS, using Global
                  keyword) 
In a Visual Basic application, only use global variables when there is no other convenient way to share data between forms. You may want to consider storing information in a control's Tag property, which can be accessed globally using the form.object.property syntax. 

If you must use global variables, it is good practice to declare all of them in a single module and group them by function. Give the module a meaningful name that indicates its purpose, such as GLOBAL.BAS. 

With the exception of global variables (which should not be passed), procedures and functions should only operate on objects that are passed to them. Global variables that are used in routines should be identified in the general comment area at the beginning of the routine. In addition, pass arguments to subs and functions using ByVal, unless you explicitly want to change the value of the passed argument. 

Write modular code whenever possible. For example, if your application displays a dialog box, put all the controls and code required to perform the dialog's task in a single form. This helps to keep the application's code organized into useful components and minimizes its runtime overhead.

' ==========================================================================================
' Name              modCache - CacheString
'
' Parameters
'       Name                     (I) Variant
'       Value                    (I) String
'
' Returns
'      boolean
'
' Synopsis:
'
'
' Design Details:
'
'
' ==========================================================================================
Public Function CacheString(ByVal Name As String, ByVal Value As String) As Boolean
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler

    Dim spmMgr As COMSVCSLib.SharedPropertyGroupManager
    Dim spmGroup As COMSVCSLib.SharedPropertyGroup
    Dim spmProp As COMSVCSLib.SharedProperty
    Dim bExists As Boolean
    Dim ErrorNum As Long
    
    Const SOURCENAME = "modCache::CacheString"
    
    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "Entering modCache.CacheString StringName: '" & Name & "'")
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "ThreadID: " & App.ThreadID)
    #End If
    
    CacheString = False

    ' Validate input parameters
    If Trim(Name) = "" Then
        Err.Raise ERR_CACHEINVALIDPARM, , "Cache key name was not supplied."
    ElseIf Trim(Value) = "" Then
        Err.Raise ERR_CACHEINVALIDPARM, , "Cache key value was not supplied."
    End If
    
    ' Get reference to SPM manager
    If Not SafeCreateObject(spmMgr, %%Application Name%%_COMSVCS_SPGM, ErrorNum) Then
        'exit because SPM was not created
        GoTo ErrorHandler
    End If
        
    If (spmMgr Is Nothing) Or ErrorNum <> 0 Then
        ' this particular cache item has not yet been cached
        GoTo ErrorHandler
    End If
        
    ' Attempt to create property group -- if exists already, will simply return reference
    Set spmGroup = spmMgr.CreatePropertyGroup(%%Application Name%%_CACHEGROUPNAME, CACHEISOMODE, CACHERELEASEMODE, bExists)

    If spmGroup Is Nothing Then
        GoTo ErrorHandler
    End If
    
    ' Attempt to create property
    Set spmProp = spmGroup.CreateProperty(Name, bExists)

    If spmProp Is Nothing Then
        GoTo ErrorHandler
    End If
    
    ' Store value in new/existing property
    spmProp.Value = Value
    
    CacheString = True

CleanExit:
    Set spmProp = Nothing
    Set spmGroup = Nothing
    Set spmMgr = Nothing
    
    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "Leaving modCache.CacheString - SUCCESS")
    #End If
    
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
' To Do: Add code to try to handle the Error if applicable

'If not Handled then Destroy all objects created and Raise the Error

    Set spmProp = Nothing
    Set spmGroup = Nothing
    Set spmMgr = Nothing

    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "Leaving modCache.CacheString - FAILURE")
    #End If

    Exit Function

End Function

Public Function GetString(ByVal Name As String) As String
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler

    Dim spmMgr As COMSVCSLib.SharedPropertyGroupManager
    Dim spmGroup As COMSVCSLib.SharedPropertyGroup
    Dim spmProp As COMSVCSLib.SharedProperty
    Dim ErrorNum As Long

    Const SOURCENAME = "modCache::GetString"

    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "Entering modCache.GetString StringName: '" & Name & "'")
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "ThreadID: " & App.ThreadID)
    #End If

    GetString = ""

    ' Validate input parameters
    If Name = "" Then
        Err.Raise ERR_CACHEINVALIDPARM, , "Cache key name was not supplied."
    End If

    ' Get reference to SPM manager
    If Not SafeCreateObject(spmMgr, %%Application Name%%_COMSVCS_SPGM, ErrorNum) Then
        'exit because SPM was not created
        GoTo CleanExit
    End If

    If spmMgr Is Nothing Or ErrorNum <> 0 Then
        'error occurred create SP Group Manager
        Exit Function
    End If

    Set spmGroup = spmMgr.Group(%%Application Name%%_CACHEGROUPNAME)

    If (spmGroup Is Nothing) Then
        ' there are no cache items yet cached -- entire group does not exist
        GoTo CleanExit
    End If

    ' attempt to retrieve specific property
    Set spmProp = spmGroup.Property(Name)

    If spmProp Is Nothing Then
        ' this particular cache item has not yet been cached
        GoTo CleanExit
    End If
        
    ' Return value
    GetString = spmProp.Value
    
CleanExit:
    Set spmProp = Nothing
    Set spmGroup = Nothing
    Set spmMgr = Nothing
    
    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "Leaving modCache.GetString - SUCCESS")
    #End If
    
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
' To Do: Add code to try to handle the Error if applicable

'If not Handled then Destroy all objects created and Raise the Error

    Set spmProp = Nothing
    Set spmGroup = Nothing
    Set spmMgr = Nothing

    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "Leaving modCache.GetString - FAILURE")
    #End If

    Exit Function
End Function

Public Function GetConnectString() As String
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    
    Dim sConnect As String
    Dim ctx As ObjectContext
    
    #If DebugVersion Then
        Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "Entering modCache.GetConnectString()")
    #End If
        
    Set ctx = GetObjectContext()
    
    'Caching is only enabled when object is in a package
    If Not ctx Is Nothing Then
        GetConnectString = GetString(DEFAULTCONNECTNAME)
    End If
    
    If GetConnectString = "" Then
        ' My Computer\HKCU\Software\VB and VBA Program Settings\
        sConnect = GetSetting(APPLICATIONNAME, "Database", "ConnectString")
        
        If sConnect = "" Then
            Call SaveSetting(APPLICATIONNAME, "Database", "ConnectString", DEFAULTCONNECTSTRING)
            sConnect = DEFAULTCONNECTSTRING
        End If
                    
        GetConnectString = sConnect
                
        If Not ctx Is Nothing Then
            'IF RUNNING THIS THRU THE WEB YOU NEED TO GRANT SECURITY ACCESS
            Call CacheString(DEFAULTCONNECTNAME, sConnect)
        End If
    End If
    
CleanExit:
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
' To Do: Add code to try to handle the Error if applicable

'If not Handled then Destroy all objects created and Raise the Error
    Dim lErrLine As Long
    Dim lErrNumber As Long
    Dim strErrSource As String
    Dim strErrDescription As String

    'Preserve Error Information
    lErrNumber = Err.Number
    lErrLine = Erl
    strErrSource = Err.Source
    strErrDescription = Err.Description

    Call HandleException("", lErrNumber, strErrDescription, lErrLine, strErrSource)
    Exit Function
    
End Function

' ==========================================================================================
' Name              modDataAccess - ParseParameters
'
' Parameters
'       cm                          (I/0)  ADODB.Command
'       Parameters                  (I) Variant()
'       ErrorParmIndex              (I/O) Long
'       ErrorNum                    (I/O) Long
'
' Returns
'      boolean
'
' Synopsis:
'
'
' Design Details:
'
'
' ==========================================================================================
Public Function ParseParameters(cm As Command, Parameters As Variant, ErrorParmIndex As Long, ErrorNum As Long) As Boolean
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    
    Dim prm As ADODB.Parameters
    Dim inx As Long
    Dim parse As Boolean
    
    ParseParameters = False
    
    Set prm = cm.Parameters
    
    If Not cm Is Nothing Then
        'Add the default return value
        prm.Append cm.CreateParameter("RETURN_VALUE", adInteger, adParamReturnValue, 0)
        
        For inx = LBound(Parameters, 2) To UBound(Parameters, 2)
            parse = True
            prm.Append cm.CreateParameter(Parameters(PARMNAME, inx), Parameters(PARMTYPE, inx), Parameters(PARMDIR, inx), Parameters(PARMLENGTH, inx), Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx))
            parse = False
        Next inx
    End If
    
    ParseParameters = True
    
CleanExit:
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
    Set prm = Nothing

    If parse Then
         ErrorNum = SQL_BADPARAMETERVALUE
    Else
         ErrorNum = Err.Number
    End If

    ErrorParmIndex = inx
    ParseParameters = False
    
    Exit Function
    
End Function

' ==========================================================================================
' Name              modDataAccess - ParseRefreshParameters
'
' Parameters
'       cm                          (I/0)  ADODB.Command
'       Parameters                  (I) Variant()
'       ErrorParmIndex              (I/O) Long
'       ErrorNum                    (I/O) Long
'
' Returns
'      boolean
'
' Synopsis:
'
'
' Design Details:
'
'
' ==========================================================================================
Public Function ParseRefreshParameters(cm As Command, Parameters As Variant, ErrorParmIndex As Long, ErrorNum As Long) As Boolean
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    
    Dim inx As Long
    Dim prm As ADODB.Parameter
    Dim sStep As String

    ParseRefreshParameters = False
    
    If Not cm Is Nothing And Not IsEmptyArray(Parameters) Then
        For inx = LBound(Parameters, 2) To UBound(Parameters, 2)
            If Len(Trim(Parameters(PARMNAME, inx))) > 0 Then
                sStep = "P"
                Set prm = cm.Parameters(Parameters(PARMNAME, inx))
                sStep = ""
                If Not IsEmpty(Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx)) Then
                    sStep = "V"
                    prm.Value = Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx)
                    sStep = ""
                End If
            End If
            Set prm = Nothing
        Next inx
    End If
    
    ParseRefreshParameters = True
    
CleanExit:
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
    Set prm = Nothing

    If sStep = "P" Then
         ErrorNum = SQL_BADPARAMETERNAME
    ElseIf sStep = "V" Then
         ErrorNum = SQL_BADPARAMETERVALUE
    Else
         ErrorNum = Err.Number
    End If

    ErrorParmIndex = inx
    
    ParseRefreshParameters = False
      
    Exit Function
        
End Function
' ==========================================================================================
' Name              modDataAccess - UnParseParameters
'
' Parameters
'       cm                          (I/0)  ADODB.Command
'       Parameters                  (I/O) Variant()
'
' Returns
'      boolean
'
' Synopsis:
'
'
' Design Details:
'
'
' ==========================================================================================
Public Function UnParseParameters(cm As Command, Parameters As Variant) As Boolean
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler
    
    Dim inx As Long
    
    If cm.Parameters.Count = 0 Then
        Parameters = Empty
        UnParseParameters = True
        GoTo CleanExit
    End If

    ReDim Parameters(RETURN_PARMUBOUND, cm.Parameters.Count - 1)
    
    For inx = 0 To cm.Parameters.Count - 1
        Parameters(RETURN_PARMNAME, inx) = cm.Parameters.Item(inx).Name
        Parameters(RETURN_PARMVALUE, inx) = cm.Parameters.Item(inx).Value
    Next inx
    
    UnParseParameters = True
    
CleanExit:
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
    UnParseParameters = False
    Exit Function
    
End Function

            'Create a ADO recordset object
            If Not SafeCreateObject(rs, %%Application Name%%_ADODB_RECORDSET, ErrorNum) Then
                Err.Raise DA_CREATEADORECORDSETFAILED, SOURCENAME, "Unable to create ADODB.Recordset. Return Code was " & ErrorNum
                GoTo CleanExit
            End If

            'Set the recordset properties
            rs.CursorLocation = adUseClient
                        
            If ReturnDataType = dtRecordset And (DataDirection = adInputOutput Or DataDirection = adOutput) Then
                'Open the recordset as Static then the receiver and move around in the rs
                rs.Open cm, , adOpenStatic, adLockReadOnly
            Else
                'Open the recordset as ForwardOnly since this will return a variant
                rs.Open cm, , adOpenForwardOnly, adLockReadOnly
            End If
    
        Case etSQL
            'Create ADO command object for stored procedures calls
            If Not SafeCreateObject(cn, %%Application Name%%_ADODB_CONNECT, ErrorNum) Then
                Err.Raise DA_CREATEADOCONNECTFAILED, SOURCENAME, "Unable to create ADODB.Connection. Return Code was " & ErrorNum
                GoTo CleanExit
            End If
                         
            'Set environment settings
            cn.ConnectionString = ConstructString
            cn.CursorLocation = adUseClient
            cn.Open
            
            If DataDirection = adUnknown Or DataDirection = adInput Then
                'This will return no data
                cn.Execute ExecuteText, lRowsAffected, adExecuteNoRecords
            Else
                'This will return a recordset
                Set rs = cn.Execute(ExecuteText, lRowsAffected)
            End If
        
        Case Else
            Err.Raise DA_UNVALIDEXECUTETYPE, SOURCENAME, "Invalid execute type."
            GoTo CleanExit
    
    End Select
        
    'Check for errors
    If Not cn Is Nothing Then
        If cn.Errors.Count <> 0 Then
            Err.Raise DA_SOURCEERROR, SOURCENAME, "Execution failed."
            GoTo CleanExit
        End If
    End If
    
    'Copy the output parameters back into the variant array
    If (ParmDirection = adOutput Or ParmDirection = adInputOutput) And _
            Not IsMissing(Parameters) Then
        'Verify command is still open to retrieve the return parameters
        If rs.State = adStateClosed Then
            'clear parameters since command was closed
            Erase Parameters
        Else
            'Copy return parameters
            If ExecutionType = etSQL Then
                ReDim Parameters(1, 0)
                Parameters(0, 0) = "@RowCount"
                Parameters(1, 0) = lRowsAffected
            Else
                If Not UnParseParameters(cm, Parameters) Then
                    Err.Raise DA_UNPARSEPARAMETERSFAILED, SOURCENAME, "Error occurred un-parsing parameters."
                    GoTo CleanExit
                End If
            End If
        End If
    Else
        If Not IsEmptyArray(Parameters) Then
            Erase Parameters
        End If
    End If
        
    If (DataDirection = adInputOutput Or DataDirection = adOutput) And _
            Not IsMissing(Data) Then
        Select Case ReturnDataType
            Case dtRecordset
                If rs.State = adStateClosed Then
                    Set rs = Nothing
                    Set Data = Nothing
                Else
                    Set rs.ActiveConnection = Nothing
                    Set Data = rs
                End If

            Case dtXML
                'Need to code
            
            Case dtVariant
                If rs.State = adStateClosed Then
                    Set rs = Nothing
                    Set Data = Nothing
                Else
                    Set rs.ActiveConnection = Nothing
                    If rs.RecordCount > 0 Then
                        Data = rs.GetRows
                        
                        'Add the columns names to the end of the array
                        LastRow = UBound(Data, 2) + 1
                        ReDim Preserve Data(UBound(Data, 1), LastRow)
                        For inx = 0 To rs.Fields.Count - 1
                            Data(inx, LastRow) = rs.Fields.Item(inx).Name
                        Next inx
                    Else
                        Set Data = Nothing
                    End If
                End If
                                    
            Case dtString
                Data = rs.GetString(adClipString)
                Set rs.ActiveConnection = Nothing
        
        End Select
    End If
                          
    'Clean up the command object after parsing the parameters
    If Not cm Is Nothing Then
        Set cm.ActiveConnection = Nothing
        Set cm = Nothing
    End If
        
    Execute = True
         
CleanExit:
%%Include::1,ECC MSDN Elements - DebugInfo SetComplete%%

    'Clean up
    Set cn = Nothing
    Set rs = Nothing
    Set cm = Nothing

%%Include::1,ECC MSDN Elements - DebugInfo Success%%
    
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:

    Dim lErrNumber As Long
    Dim lErrLine As Long
    Dim strErrSource As String
    Dim strErrDescription As String
    Dim strTemp As String
    Dim strValue As String
    
    'Preserve it before we do IsEmptyArray
    lErrNumber = Err.Number
    lErrLine = Erl
    strErrSource = Err.Source
    strErrDescription = Err.Description
                    
    strTemp = vbCrLf & "     SOURCE: " & strErrSource & _
            vbCrLf & "     STORED PROCEDURE: " & ExecuteText & _
            vbCrLf & "     DESCRIPTION: " & strErrDescription & vbCrLf
            
    If IsMissing(Parameters) Then
        strTemp = strTemp & "     PARAMETERS: None"
    ElseIf IsEmptyArray(Parameters) Then
        strTemp = strTemp & "     PARAMETERS: None"
    Else
        strTemp = strTemp & "     PARAMETERS: " & vbCrLf
        For inx = LBound(Parameters, 2) To UBound(Parameters, 2)
            If IsNull(Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx)) Then
                strValue = "<NULL>"
            ElseIf UCase(Parameters(PARMNAME, inx)) = "@RECORDTIMESTAMP" Then
                Dim strTS As String
                strTS = TimestampToString(Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx))
                If strTS = "" Then
                    strValue = "<NONE>"
                Else
                    strValue = strTS
                End If
            ElseIf TypeName(Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx)) = "Byte()" Then
                strValue = "Byte()"
            ElseIf Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx) = "" Then
                strValue = "''"
            ElseIf IsEmpty(Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx)) Then
                strValue = "<EMPTY>"
            ElseIf IsNumeric(Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx)) Then
                strValue = Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx)
            ElseIf IsDate(Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx)) Then
                strValue = Format(Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx), STANDARDDATEFORMAT)
            Else
                strValue = Parameters(PARMVALUE, inx)
            End If
            
            strTemp = strTemp & "     " & Parameters(PARMNAME, inx) & " = " & strValue & vbCrLf
        Next inx
    End If

    Set rs = Nothing
    Set cm = Nothing
    Set cn = Nothing

    #If DebugVersion Then
        'Error occurred therefore makes sure the context is marked aborted
        If Not ctx Is Nothing Then
            ctx.SetAbort
            Call OutputDebugString(DebugPrefix & "I%%Application Name%%DataAccessEng.Execute - SetAbort - ExecuteText = " & ExecuteText)
            Set ctx = Nothing
        End If
    #End If
    
%%Include::1,ECC MSDN Elements - DebugInfo Failure%%    

    Call HandleException(SecurityToken, lErrNumber, strTemp, lErrLine, SOURCENAME, False, strErrSource)
    Exit Function
